Decades of unplanned growth have produced a city of narrow lanes, ageing unreinforced masonry, illegally altered ground floors, and utility lines that snake through walls and under footpaths with almost no protective control. Most existing responses to this danger treat the problem in isolated pieces: planners talk about widening roads, engineers talk about strengthening columns, and utility agencies talk about pipeline maintenance, but rarely do these three conversations happen at the same table. This paper argues that earthquake loss in a historic unplanned city cannot be meaningfully reduced unless spatial planning, structural retrofitting, and utility-safety engineering are treated as one connected system rather than three separate departments. Using a mixed-method approach that combines a review of Bangladeshi and international case evidence, secondary structural and demographic data from RAJUK, BNBC 2020, WASA, and DESCO/DPDC-type utility records, and a GIS-informed spatial reading of a representative Old Dhaka ward, the paper builds an Integrated Resilience Framework with four connected components: (i) micro-scale spatial replanning that opens rescue corridors and pocket assembly points without demolishing the historic fabric; (ii) low-disruption structural strengthening using fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) wrapping, jacketing, and soft-storey correction; (iii) a smart utility-safety layer built on Internet of Things (IoT) seismic sensors that trigger automatic gas and electricity shut-off, paired with flexible high-density polyethylene (HDPE) water piping; and (iv) a comparative loss-estimation exercise that places the "do nothing" scenario against the integrated intervention scenario. The comparative analysis, built from published vulnerability studies of Dhaka together with international retrofitting performance data, suggests that, on this paper's own illustrative loss-index synthesis, a fully integrated programme could plausibly reduce combined structural, fire, and utility-related casualties and economic loss by roughly 80% relative to the current trajectory-compared with an estimated 48% reduction from structural retrofit alone-although these are order-of-magnitude estimates from a literature-based synthesis, not a calibrated simulation, and the precise number depends heavily on how much of the Old Dhaka Seismic Risk Integrated Planning-Construction-Utility Resilience Framework programme is actually implemented and maintained. The paper closes with policy recommendations for RAJUK, the two Dhaka City Corporations, and the Fire Service and Civil Defence, and argues that public-private partnership and genuine participation of Old Dhaka's residents are what will decide whether this framework survives on paper or changes real outcomes on the ground.

title: The Energy Base: Why Labor Taxes Should Be Replaced with an Energy Tax

detail.title: The Energy Base: Why Labor Taxes Should Be Replaced with an Energy Tax
detail.abstract:
Modern states fund themselves by taxing labor income. That base is a historical artifact of an economy in which labor performed most production. It now yields substantially less revenue than the obligations it funds require. The United States collected approximately 5.2 trillion dollars against 7.0 trillion of spending in fiscal 2025 — at the end of an expansion. Closing that gap on the existing base means raising receipts by about a third, to roughly 23 percent of GDP — a level never reached in any postwar year across rates ranging from a 91 percent top bracket to a 28 percent one.

This paper argues that the tax base should move from labor to primary energy. It provides a concrete framework to achieve that transition with minimal economic disruption, and to pay off the federal debt in about a generation.

The argument is not only about revenue. A tax applies downward pressure on the use of whatever it is levied on. The choice of base therefore decides what an economy is discouraged from using, and moving that pressure off labor and onto energy should raise the relative value of employing people while rewarding efficiency in the use of energy.

The instrument is a levy on energy entering the economy — at extraction, at non-combustion generation, and at the border — charged at a published rate that rises on a fixed schedule. Border adjustment runs in both directions, removing a penalty American producers carry today. A dividend is paid per capita, at a rate selected to offset the energy a household buys directly.

The base is approximately 99.5 quadrillion BTU: 88 entering domestically, plus about 11.5 embodied in imported goods net of the rebate on exports. On a two-cent-a-year schedule the requirement closes in year 18 at thirty-six cents per delivered kilowatt-hour-equivalent — yielding on the order of 10.5 trillion dollars against a 30.7 trillion dollar economy. That retires roughly 4.3 trillion dollars of individual income and payroll taxes.

The case rests on three properties of energy and no others: it is universal (embodied in all production), meterable (at a small number of fixed physical points), and unavoidable (no production without it). It does not rest on energy being a large share of costs or on any particular timetable for automation.

All figures derive from a published constants module and an interactive model, both cited and public. Every assumption behind them is a control the reader can move. The whole run exports as data.

title: The Three-Way Complementarity Between Automation, Profit Sharing, And Training: Theory and Evidence
affiliations: Università di Parma, University of Turin and University of Parma - Dipartimento di Scienze Economiche e Aziendali

detail.title: The Three-Way Complementarity Between Automation, Profit Sharing, And Training: Theory and Evidence
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the complementarity between automation, profit sharing, and digital training. We develop a team-theoretic model in which a principal manages two technologically interdependent tasks, one of which can be automated. Because only joint output can be observed, incentives must be provided through profit sharing. By improving team performance, automation increases the cost of incentive provision under profit sharing, generating a tension between the two practices. Training counteracts this effect by increasing the marginal productivity of effort, thereby reducing the cost of incentive provision. Three predictions follow: training and automation are always complementary, profit sharing and automation may be either complements or substitutes, and the three practices are jointly complementary. Reduced-form evidence from a sample of Italian firms supports these predictions: blue-collar profit sharing and digital training are individually associated with robot adoption, but part of these associations is captured by their interaction. The interaction disappears for non-IT training, white-collar profit sharing, and a wide range of non-automation technologies, indicating a complementarity specific to human-machine production.

title:
Privacy Is Not Enough
On Identity, Agentic AI, and What We Are Actually Losing

detail.title:
Privacy Is Not Enough
On Identity, Agentic AI, and What We Are Actually Losing

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of Grio and the creator of Codexes.ai, a platform that implements the boundary-first architectural principles described in this essay. This represents a potential non-financial competing interest. The author declares no financial interests related to the submission of this manuscript. This paper has been submitted for peer review to AI & Society (Springer Open Forum, August 2026).
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a philosophical position paper with no human participants, patient data, or empirical studies.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this work.

detail.abstract: Privacy law was built to protect data. But the emergence of persistent, context-aggregating agentic AI systems poses a threat that data protection cannot address: the reduction of a person's plural, context-dependent identity to a single statistical composite. This essay introduces the concept of cognitive identity capture-the process by which an agentic AI system, through the accumulation of personal context across all domains of a person's life, constructs and imposes a unified model of who that person is, undermining their capacity to be different people in different contexts. Drawing on Kant's account of autonomy, Clark and Chalmers' extended mind thesis, Nissenbaum's contextual integrity framework, Illich's distinction between convivial and non-convivial tools, and Damasio and McGaugh's neuroscience of selective memory, the essay argues that cognitive identity capture constitutes a distinct harm-one that is structural, architectural, and prior to any question of data ownership or compensation. Against Lanier's Data Dignity proposal, which addresses the terms of extraction, this essay addresses the need for extraction itself. It proposes three rights that current legal frameworks do not provide: the right to be plural, the right to be unlearned, and the right to determine, in each context, which version of oneself is present. It concludes with a set of architectural conditions-local-first context storage, identity-bounded domains, model-agnostic context management, and explicit bridges-that define what a convivial AI system requires. The essay is written in the first person, as a position piece in the Open Forum tradition, grounded in both academic literature and the author's practice as an AI strategist, educator, and researcher.

title: Beyond Spiritual Intelligence: Toward a General Theory of Spiritual Cognition
affiliations: African Research Network (ARN)

detail.title: Beyond Spiritual Intelligence: Toward a General Theory of Spiritual Cognition
detail.abstract: Spiritual intelligence has emerged as an important concept at the intersection of psychology, leadership, education, and organizational studies. However, the field remains conceptually fragmented, with competing definitions, inconsistent theoretical assumptions, and limited integration with recent developments in cognitive science and neuroscience. This article argues that the notion of spiritual intelligence should be reconceptualized within a broader framework of spiritual cognition, defined as the set of higher-order cognitive processes through which individuals construct meaning, discern values, anticipate future possibilities, cultivate relational awareness, and orient action toward transcendent purposes. Rather than treating spirituality as an isolated psychological trait, the proposed theory positions spiritual cognition as an adaptive cognitive architecture emerging from the dynamic interaction of embodied experience, predictive cognition, moral reasoning, relational consciousness, and reflective self-transcendence. By integrating advances in predictive processing, embodied cognition, the cognitive science of religion, moral psychology, phenomenology, neosology, complexity science, and contemporary neuroscience, the article proposes a unified conceptual model capable of explaining how spiritual cognition contributes to ethical judgment, resilient leadership, creativity, and human flourishing. The resulting framework provides a new interdisciplinary foundation for empirical research while extending current debates beyond conventional models of spiritual intelligence. It offers a theoretically robust platform for future investigations across theology, psychology, leadership studies, organizational science, and the cognitive sciences.

title: Ready for what? Enlistment versus Readiness

detail.title: Ready for what? Enlistment versus Readiness

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is a readiness specialist at the Spanish Ministry of Defense. He has carried out eight international missions. During his 2012 mission in Iraq, under NATO auspices, he served as an advisor to the Iraqi Lieutenant General responsible for readiness.
declarations.funderStatement: The article was published by the Journal of the Spanish Institute of Strategic Studies of the Spanish Ministry of Defense due to its interest

detail.abstract: The fundamental purpose of Armed Forces is to fight and win a Nation's conflicts. Therefore, it is critical that Ministers of Defence (MoD) continually assesses warfighting readiness and capabilities. Readiness is the ability of Armed Forces to conduct and successfully accomplish assigned missions as specified in the National Military Strategy (NMS) with sufficient and sustainable capabilities resulting from personnel, equipment, training, and supporting infrastructures. The readiness system provides an overall assessment of the Ministry of Defence's (MoD) ability to execute the NMS and captures the overarching readiness for each level of warfighting. History holds numerous examples of the cost nations have paid when their Armed Forces were not prepared to respond. Next, the concept of International Readiness is shown, its extrapolation to the Spanish environment and some examples of Readiness systems implemented in other countries are analyzed. This article concludes with the future challenges that are presented to these Readiness evaluation systems in the coming years.

title: Beyond Obsolescence: Dependency Analysis as Cornerstone of Global South Political Economy in the Multipolar Era

detail.title: Beyond Obsolescence: Dependency Analysis as Cornerstone of Global South Political Economy in the Multipolar Era
detail.abstract: Dependency theory is frequently dismissed as obsolete, yet the paradox of intensified structural constraints during Western hegemonic decline suggests otherwise. This article argues that classical Marxist dependency theory-developed by Baran, Amin, Marini, Dos Santos, and Bambirra-provides indispensable analytical tools for understanding contemporary global capitalism. Drawing on recent scholarship on subordinate financialization, global value chains, and monetary hierarchy, we demonstrate how dependency mechanisms persist and intensify through increasingly sophisticated forms that appear voluntary and market-driven. The article develops an original analytical framework comprising two complementary indices: the Structural Dependency Index (SDI), which measures multidimensional constraints across commercial, technological, financial, productive, network, and distributive dimensions; and the State Mediating Capacity (SMC), which captures institutional resources for navigating these constraints. This dual framework generates a four-quadrant typology-Non-Hegemonic Autonomy, Hegemonic Centers, Subordinate Periphery, and Contested Semi-Periphery-that enables systematic comparison across economies while identifying transformation pathways. Both indices are presented here as a proposed operationalization: their dimensions, component variables and data sources are fully specified, but the indices have not yet been computed, and the country placements reported below are theoretically derived rather than empirically estimated. Drawing on Poulantzas and Mann, we clarify the qualitatively distinct meanings of state capacity in core and peripheral economies. The multipolar transition creates opportunities for autonomous development, but realizing these opportunities requires state capacity adequate to strategic delinking-a transformation that historically depends on bottom-up political coalitions capable of challenging entrenched class interests.

title: Digital System Design Transitions: From Boolean Minimization to Programmable Logic Implementations
affiliations: Bulacan State University

detail.title: Digital System Design Transitions: From Boolean Minimization to Programmable Logic Implementations
detail.abstract: This paper examines the transition from Boolean logic minimization to programmable logic implementation in industrial automation, with particular emphasis on Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) ladder programming. It explores how fundamental digital logic concepts, including Boolean algebra, logic gates, and logic simplification, can be translated into practical ladder logic programs used in automated manufacturing systems. The study critically evaluates the role of Boolean minimization in reducing unnecessary logic elements, improving program organization, and potentially enhancing PLC memory utilization and execution efficiency. A theoretical and functional modeling approach is used to compare simplified Boolean expressions with their corresponding ladder logic implementations. The analysis demonstrates that a strong understanding of digital logic provides an important foundation for developing efficient and maintainable PLC programs. However, the reviewed discussion is primarily focused on conventional relay-based ladder logic and provides limited empirical evidence regarding differences in execution performance among PLC platforms. The paper therefore recommends incorporating actual PLC scan-time measurements, memory usage comparisons, and evaluations across different PLC manufacturers in future studies. Overall, the paper highlights the continuing importance of Boolean logic minimization in industrial automation education and PLC-based control system development.

reference: Accepted for publication by the Journal for Financial Education
title: A Classroom Experience to Introduce Behavioral Finance and Anchoring Bias
affiliations: Seton Hall University - Department of Finance & Legal Studies and Ipsos Behavioral Science Center

detail.title: A Classroom Experience to Introduce Behavioral Finance and Anchoring Bias

publicationDetails.detailsText: Accepted for publication by the Journal for Financial Education

detail.abstract:
This paper presents an interactive classroom experiment designed to introduce students to behavioral finance and anchoring bias. Anchoring, a well-documented behavioral bias, occurs when an initial value subconsciously influences subsequent judgments. The exercise, based on the seminal work of Tversky and Kahneman (1974), demonstrates the pervasive impact of anchoring bias, challenging the assumptions of rational decision-making foundational to traditional economic theory. 

The experiment begins with a brief survey administered to randomly divided student groups, where the initial question contains an arbitrary anchor. By comparing group responses to a subsequent question, students observe the bias in their own judgments. Results consistently reveal significant anchoring effects, stimulating introspection and active class discussions. This hands-on approach facilitates deep engagement and enhances students' comprehension of behavioral concepts. Feedback from students underscores the experiment's effectiveness in making abstract concepts relatable and memorable.

title: Generic Gains from Money Creation: General Results

detail.title: Generic Gains from Money Creation: General Results
detail.abstract: This paper proves a Wallace theorem for nominally homogeneous purecurrency economies under anticipated permanent money creation. The Implementation Theorem shows that a proportional, welfare-neutral transfer can be added to any locally favorable policy direction to obtain a nonnegative, increasing policy that is truthfully implemented with private balances. The Genericity Theorem shows that, within a finite-dimensional family of nonproportional policy directions, failure of first-order welfare improvement is confined to a lower-dimensional exceptional set under a full-rank condition. A three-type Lagos-Wright economy verifies all assumptions from primitives and identifies an open parameter region with a strictly welfare-improving permanent transfer policy.

reference: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21843591
title: Adjudication of LGBTI Rights in Malawi

detail.title: Adjudication of LGBTI Rights in Malawi
detail.abstract:
This article critically examines the judicial adjudication of LGBTI rights in Malawi
through a comparative analysis of two landmark constitutional cases: R v Steven
Monjeza Soko and Tiwonge Chimbalanga Kachapa (2010) and Jan Willem Akster
and Jana Gonani v DPP and Attorney General (2024). Despite Malawi's ratification of
major international human rights instruments, including the International Covenant on
Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) and the African Charter on Human and Peoples'
Rights, Section 153 of the Penal Code continues to criminalise "carnal knowledge
against the order of nature"—a provision inherited from British colonial rule. The
study employs the FILAC (Facts, Issues, Law, Analysis, Conclusion) framework to
interrogate how Malawian courts have interpreted constitutional guarantees of
equality, dignity, privacy, and personal liberty in cases involving same-sex conduct.
The analysis reveals a consistent judicial approach characterised by: (i) restrictive
constitutional interpretation that declines to read "sexual orientation" into Section 20's
non-discrimination clause; (ii) significant deference to societal morality and cultural
norms over individual constitutional rights; (iii) limited engagement with comparative
jurisprudence from progressive jurisdictions such as South Africa and India; and (iv) a
dualist approach to international law that renders treaty obligations non-binding
without domestic legislative incorporation. In both cases, the courts upheld the
constitutionality of anti-sodomy laws, reasoning that the omission of "sexual
orientation" from the Constitution reflects deliberate constitutional choice, and
advising litigants to seek legislative reform through Parliament.
The article argues that Malawi's judicial approach raises fundamental questions about
the protection of minority rights against majoritarian sentiment, the role of courts in
advancing constitutional morality, and the tension between colonial-era laws and
modern constitutional principles. It further examines the limited impact of civil
society advocacy, the fragility of executive initiatives such as President Joyce Banda's
2012 moratorium on arrests, and the significant obstacles to legislative reform posed
by deeply entrenched societal opposition, reflected in surveys showing over 90%
intolerance toward same-sex relationships. The study concludes that meaningful
progress toward decriminalisation and equality for LGBT Malawians requires not
only legal reform but broader societal change, and that while courts have directed
litigants to Parliament, political and religious opposition presents formidable barriers
to legislative action.

title: Drawing a Distinction: Modeling Paradoxical Tensions in Patterns

detail.title: Drawing a Distinction: Modeling Paradoxical Tensions in Patterns
detail.abstract: Patterns capture recurring solutions to problems that arise in a context, but at the heart of each pattern lies a tension between complementary but opposing forces. Such tensions are commonly treated as trade-offs, resolved by choosing one force over the other. In many cases, however, they are paradoxes that cannot be resolved, only managed. This paper models paradoxical tensions explicitly, representing them as forms: configurations of nested distinctions that can fold back on themselves to keep a tension open rather than settle it (a re-entrant form). Each pattern's central tension, together with the pair of actions that manage it, is represented as a pair of such re-entrant forms. Because each pattern's tension is itself a distinction, applying one pattern within another nests their tensions. This framework is demonstrated with patterns for open source business each organized around a distinct paradoxical tension. The result is a notation for patterns as ongoing, self-renegotiating processes that manage their tensions rather than settle them.

title: Philanthropy Along the Supply Chain
affiliations: Monash University - Department of Banking and Finance, Monash University, Monash University and Business School, University of Sydney, Sydney, New South Wales, Australia, 2000

detail.title: Philanthropy Along the Supply Chain
detail.abstract: How do firms sustain cooperation across firm boundaries when contracts are incomplete? Combining data on interfirm trade links, nonprofit affiliations, and corporate donations, we document that firms allocate discretionary resources to organizations affiliated with insiders of economically important, active supply chain partners. Identification tests exploiting supplier shocks and supplier-CEO turnover indicate firms reallocate resources tracking trading relationship status, strength, and decision-makers. Donations concentrate in nonprofits where they provide the most value to supplier insiders, and are associated with greater trade credit, technological alignment, and partnership initiation. Our results highlight how informal nonmarket mechanisms can influence trade relations and firm boundaries.

title: Mapping the Research Structure of Financial Behavior in Southeast Asia: A Bibliometric Review
affiliations: Rizal Technological University and University of the Philippines College of Law

detail.title: Mapping the Research Structure of Financial Behavior in Southeast Asia: A Bibliometric Review
detail.abstract: This study presents a bibliometric analysis of financial behavior research in Southeast Asia from 2020 to 2025, aiming to map its intellectual structure, research trends, and emerging themes. Using data retrieved from the Open Alex database and analyzed through VOS viewer and Bibliometrix, the study examines publication growth, influential authors, journals, institutions, and collaborative networks. Findings reveal a rapid increase in research output, with Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore leading in productivity and impact. Core themes center on financial literacy, finance, business, and economics, while emerging topics include digital finance, fintech adoption, and behavioral perspectives. The analysis also highlights strong intra-regional collaboration but limited global integration. The study underscores the importance of financial behavior in promoting financial inclusion, economic stability, and individual well-being. By providing a comprehensive overview, the findings offer valuable insights for researchers, policymakers, and practitioners in developing evidence-based financial strategies in the Southeast Asian context.

title: Joint Learning of Local-Stochastic Volatility Calibration: A Projection-Constrained Neural Operator Approach

detail.title: Joint Learning of Local-Stochastic Volatility Calibration: A Projection-Constrained Neural Operator Approach
detail.abstract: Local-stochastic volatility (LSV) models combine the marginal fit of local volatility with the richer dynamics of stochastic volatility, but their calibration is governed by a circular McKean-Vlasov fixed point. This paper presents an independent implementation and controlled experimental study of the projection-constrained neural-operator architecture introduced by Wang et al. (2026). Given a finite bid-ask quote book and a stochastic-volatility backbone descriptor, the implementation returns four linked fields: log implied variance, Dupire local variance, the conditional variance moment, and squared leverage. Quote fit, static no-arbitrage margins, a division-free Dupire residual, and the Markovian-projection identity are adapted as training and evaluation constraints. A constant-variance backbone supplies an exact diagnostic benchmark before particle noise and stochastic fixed-point error are introduced. The reported single-seed run uses 40 training states and 8 complete held-out states. It produces an implied-volatility RMSE of 249.494 basis points, a leverage RMSE of 0.181662, and a mean independent flux error of 0.319633. Under the illustrative frozen thresholds, both a representative held-out state and a deliberately stressed state are rejected, respectively because of structural residual error and excessive distributional distance. These results do not establish production readiness. They show how a compact implementation can expose approximation error through linked surfaces, independent diagnostics, and selective routing rather than conceal it behind visually smooth outputs.

title: Valuing Proprietary Trading Firm Evaluation Contracts: Closed Form, Cross-Firm Dispersion and the Source of the Margin
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Valuing Proprietary Trading Firm Evaluation Contracts: Closed Form, Cross-Firm Dispersion and the Source of the Margin

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author purchased and traded the proprietary trading firm evaluation product that serves as the case study in Section 8. The author holds no financial interest in, and has received no compensation from, any firm named in this paper. No firm named was contacted, consulted, or given advance sight of the manuscript. All contractual parameters were collected from publicly accessible pages on each firm's own domain, on a stated access date.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no funding from any agency, institution, or commercial entity. It was conducted independently by the author, who bore all costs, including the purchase of the product analysed in the case study.

detail.abstract: The evaluations sold by proprietary trading firms are contracts with a bounded premium, a contingent payoff and termination by an absorbing event defined on the drawdown of the P&L. This paper derives their success probability in closed form as a chain of first-passage problems, with six contractual parameters: profit target, drawdown buffer, the level at which the barrier stops trailing, the frequency at which it is updated, the frequency at which breach is checked, and the daily loss limit. The expression reproduces simulation with an error below 1% within its range of validity, which is stated. Applied to thirteen products of the same account size collected from official sources, the success probability varies by 62% across products that advertise identical profit target and drawdown buffer. The variation comes entirely from parameters that the firms publish but not alongside the price, and that no industry comparison records. Two criteria assessable from published terms follow from the valuation: the minimum productivity that makes an evaluation worth its price, and a sufficient condition under which it is not worth it to any buyer. Carried into the unit P&L, both converge on a single figure-the break-even conversion rate-which is simultaneously the buyer's viability threshold and the point at which the seller's contribution vanishes. The pass rates the industry publishes lie below it; the one the model predicts, above. The difference implies a drift for the average buyer three to thirty times larger than any plausible execution cost, and places the origin of the margin not in the price of the contract but in the selection the evaluation performs.

title: Architectures for Adaptive and Assistive AI Systems: Multi-Agent Reasoning, Brain-Computer Interfaces, and Conversational Agents in Education and Healthcare
affiliations: , Nanyang Technological University (NTU) and Nanyang Technological University (NTU)

detail.title: Architectures for Adaptive and Assistive AI Systems: Multi-Agent Reasoning, Brain-Computer Interfaces, and Conversational Agents in Education and Healthcare

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I declare the sole authorship of this research paper
declarations.ethicsApproval: I declare the sole authorship of this research paper
declarations.funderStatement: I declare the sole authorship of this research paper
declarations.clinicalTrialRegistration: I declare the sole authorship of this research paper

detail.abstract: Systems that adapt to a user's real-time state rather than treating every user identically are being built through at least three architecturally distinct strategies: distributed multi-agent reasoning, in which specialized agents divide and cross-check a task; direct physiological signal input, as in brain-computer interfaces (BCI) that adjust content delivery to a learner's measured cognitive load; and self-improving conversational agents, which adapt through accumulated interaction rather than a sensor channel. This paper compares these three strategies as they appear in a matched set of applied systems, a multi-agent tooloriented reasoning architecture, a BCI-driven language-learning platform, and an auto-improving healthcare chatbot against the broader technical literature on each approach. It finds that the three strategies differ sharply in what "adaptation" actually means and how directly it is measured: multi-agent architectures adapt reasoning structure but rarely measure user-facing outcomes directly; BCI systems measure a physiological proxy for user state with high precision but, per the strongest available controlled study, do not yet reliably translate that precision into improved learning outcomes; and conversational agents adapt through interaction history and can be evaluated against real communication-competence criteria, but adaptation quality depends heavily on design choices that are not automatic properties of the architecture. The paper argues that "adaptive AI system" is not a single design pattern but a family of approaches with different evidentiary standards, and that comparing them directly, which the literature rarely does clarifies what claim of adaptivity a given system can actually support. This paper does not present original technical benchmarks; its contribution is a comparative synthesis grounded in independently verified sources.

title: A Price Tape Is Not an Audit Trail: Identification Limits in Public Trading Records

detail.title: A Price Tape Is Not an Audit Trail: Identification Limits in Public Trading Records

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of MSR Decode, operated by Main Street Research LLC, a research desk whose intended business is selling forensic reconstruction of prediction-market trading records. The prospective pilot audited in Section 4.2 of this paper is a published marketing surface for that business. No engagement has been sold and no revenue has been earned from this work. The author traded prediction markets on Polymarket personally between 2024 and 2026, holds no open prediction-market positions, and operates no automated trading in prediction markets. No party commissioned or compensated this paper. A full disclosure of interests appears in the paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was self-funded by the author.

detail.abstract: Public transaction feeds are routinely treated as audit trails even though they are provisioned only to describe market activity. This paper separates four increasingly demanding objects a reader may want from such a feed: a market-level price tape, a wallet's complete fill history, that wallet's trading performance, and the opportunity set available to a delayed follower. Timestamp, ticker, quantity and price identify the first, given a record in which each execution appears exactly once. They do not identify the other three, because different account histories and different profit paths can generate the same tape. A prediction-market case study shows the practical consequence: a public trade endpoint defaults to returning only the fills in which the queried wallet was the taker, and an analyst who accepts that default can observe a coherent-looking record that is materially incomplete. In our own use, the default led us to flag 4,725 markets across three wallets as apparent accounting discrepancies; re-fetched from a per-market activity endpoint, the 50 largest flagged markets for each wallet — 150 in total — reconciled 150 of 150 at the level of the market, and in the clearest single case a position that appeared to rest on a single purchase of about $17 proved to have eighty buy fills and roughly $9,979 of cost behind it — enough shares bought to cover every one of the 12,759 it redeemed at a dollar each. We then audit our own prospective pilot, which attempted the fourth and most demanding object — follower opportunity — and did not identify it: the gate that selected its wallets carried the same completeness defect documented above and a second defect that divided a lifetime numerator by a thirty-day denominator, its freeze occurred after first publication, its eligibility screen tested neither liquidity nor order acceptance, and its eligible set collapsed to three markets that all resolved on a single sporting fixture, one of them held by two of the six entries and accounting for most of the simulated result. We make no claim that following the pilot's wallets would have been profitable or unprofitable. The contribution is a claim-to-data sufficiency framework, a documented and reproducible completeness failure, and a minimum data contract for auditable performance research.

title: Grey-Zone Operations at Sea: Maritime Cyber Infrastructure as an Arena for Strategic Signalling
affiliations: and Unaffiliated Authors

detail.title: Grey-Zone Operations at Sea: Maritime Cyber Infrastructure as an Arena for Strategic Signalling
detail.abstract: Cyber operations targeting maritime infrastructure are commonly framed as technical disruptions designed to inflict physical or economic harm. This paper argues that many such incidents function instead as strategic signalling. The maritime domain’s mixed civilian-commercial structure and fragmented governance make it especially conducive to grey-zone and hybrid warfare, where strategic signalling plays a prominent role. Recognizing maritime cyber activity as strategic communication is essential for calibrated responses and escalation management. Examining cases of maritime cyber disruption from 2021–2025, this paper identifies patterns of amplified narratives, increasing use of AIS and GNSS manipulation, and evidence of preparation for future contingencies.

title: Ritual Without Reform? Sri Lanka's 2026 Integrity Oath as Symbolic Anti-Corruption Governance
affiliations: Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology

detail.title: Ritual Without Reform? Sri Lanka's 2026 Integrity Oath as Symbolic Anti-Corruption Governance
detail.abstract: This article critically examines Sri Lanka's 2026 "Integrity Oath" (Supilipanna Divuruma) initiative, launched under Presidential Secretariat Circular No. PS/CSL/Circular/8/2026 during National Integrity Week (27-31 July 2026), as a case study in symbolic anticorruption governance. Drawing on institutional theory's concept of ritualised isomorphism and the political science literature explaining why anti-corruption reforms fail in highcorruption contexts, the article develops a five-criterion evaluative framework-normative clarity, institutional alignment, enforcement credibility, cultural internalisation, and public legitimacy-and applies it to the Sri Lankan case using official circulars, government and civil-society publications, and contemporaneous media coverage. Employing a qualitative desk-research design structured through the Integrated-Flexible Approach and its 10Ps model, the analysis finds the initiative strong in agenda-setting and integrative framing but weak in demonstrated enforcement architecture, measurable indicators, and leadership accountability. The article argues that the oath functions primarily as a ritual of legitimation rather than a mechanism of behavioural change, and proposes a concrete reform agendaincluding a resourced, publicly visible complaints-and-consequences body and specific citizen-facing service standards-through which ceremonial commitment could be converted into institutional practice. The findings extend the ritualised-isomorphism literature to a South Asian public-administration setting and offer policy-relevant guidance for anti-corruption reform in comparable developing-country contexts.

title: The Transformation of the Monetary Policy Transmission Mechanism in the Context of the Introduction of Central Bank Digital Currencies: Theoretical and Applied Aspects

detail.title: The Transformation of the Monetary Policy Transmission Mechanism in the Context of the Introduction of Central Bank Digital Currencies: Theoretical and Applied Aspects
detail.abstract: The article examines the transformation of the monetary policy transmission mechanism in the context of central bank digital currency (CBDC) implementation. Based on the analysis of theoretical models and practical experience from CBDC projects in Russia, China, and the EU, the key channels of impact are identified. CBDC design is shown to be the key determinant of the nature and scale of transformation. The implementation of the CBDC creates the conditions for improving transmission efficiency in the long term, but during the transition phase it may generate «noisy» effects.

title: From Oil Discovery to Development: Contracts, Institutions, and Welfare in Guyana
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Department of Political Science, Inspiring Accounting Talent for a Sustainable Society, Ball State University, Ball State University and Washburn University School of Law

detail.title: From Oil Discovery to Development: Contracts, Institutions, and Welfare in Guyana

declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: Guyana’s 2015 offshore oil discovery and the start of commercial production in 2019 generated one of the world’s largest recent income booms. This paper asks whether that boom translated into broader, inclusive, and sustainable development. We develop a contract-to-welfare framework that links petroleum contract provisions – royalties, cost recovery, auditability, liability allocation, environmental safeguards, and decommissioning obligations – to observable development and welfare outcomes. Using synthetic control methods, we compare Guyana with weighted combinations of Latin American and Caribbean donor countries over pre-discovery, discovery/anticipation, and post-production periods. The results show a sharp distinction between income growth and broader development. GDP per capita and the HDI income component rise substantially relative to synthetic Guyana after production begins, while education, life expectancy, aggregate SDG performance, institutional indicators, and wealth concentration show weaker or mixed evidence of improvement. Measured national wealth and unadjusted Hicksian income improve, but liability-adjusted Hicksian income and welfare remain substantially less favorable once estimated decommissioning and contingent obligations are incorporated. In-space placebos, leave-one-out tests, covariate sensitivity checks, and a delayed-treatment comparison using Suriname support the interpretation that Guyana’s income divergence is linked to production rather than regional trends alone. The findings suggest that petroleum contracts should be evaluated not only by fiscal take or output growth, but by whether resource rents are converted into sustainable and broadly shared welfare.

title: Reducing Gender Gaps in Education: Evidence from Randomized National Tests and Teacher Grading
affiliations: IFAU - Institute for Labour Market Policy Evaluation, Uppsala University - Department of Economics and University of Cologne - Department of Economics

detail.title: Reducing Gender Gaps in Education: Evidence from Randomized National Tests and Teacher Grading
detail.abstract: Boys increasingly lag behind girls in educational attainment. Using Swedish administrative data, we show that the gender gap in college enrollment can largely be accounted for by differences in compulsory school GPA, and that boys receive lower grades than girls with the same national test scores in all subjects. We then exploit the fact that each school is randomly assigned one natural-science and one social-science subject in the grade 9 national tests. Because teachers administer and grade the tests themselves, they observe standardized information on student performance in some subjects, but not in others. National test assignment reduces the gender gap in teacher grades by 0.046 SD, which is around a third of the conditional gender gap. The effects of test assignment are similar for male and female teachers, visible throughout the ability distribution, and consistent with teachers updating their assessments in response to standardized information on student performance.

title: Generic Gains from Money Creation: Results for One-time Policies

detail.title: Generic Gains from Money Creation: Results for One-time Policies
detail.abstract: We establish a local implementation result for the Wallace conjecture in purecurrency economies with private, continuously valued balances. A favorable signed redistribution among positive-balance agents can be converted into a nonnegative, nondecreasing money-creation policy by adding a proportional monetary expansion. Exact nominal homogeneity makes this added component welfare neutral, preserving the first-order gain while ensuring truthful presentation. We also give a finite-rank genericity result for fixed contrast spaces. A fully specified three-type Lagos-Wright economy verifies equilibrium regularity, endogenous bounded support, truthful implementation, proportional neutrality, the welfare derivative, and a transverse one-dimensional cancellation point from explicit monetary primitives.

reference: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21817586
title: A Physics-Constrained Multi-Dimensional Revenue Intelligence Algorithm for Explainable Detection of Tax Fraud in the Mining and Petroleum Sectors of Developing Countries
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Physics-Constrained Multi-Dimensional Revenue Intelligence Algorithm for Explainable Detection of Tax Fraud in the Mining and Petroleum Sectors of Developing Countries
detail.abstract:
A mathematically rigorous framework for detecting tax fraud in the mining and petroleum sectors of resource-rich developing countries. The Multi-Dimensional Revenue Intelligence Algorithm (MDRIA) tests whether a taxpayer's reported production, costs, export praMining and petroleum activity accounts for a large share of government revenue in many resource-rich developing countries, yet audit selection in these jurisdictions still relies predominantly on rule-based indicators that evaluate each fraud channel in isolation. This paper develops the Multi-Dimensional Revenue Intelligence Algorithm (MDRIA), a mathematically explicit framework that tests whether a taxpayer’s reported production, costs, export prices, royalties, and shipments are jointly feasible given engineering identities, geological constraints, statutory parameters, and market reference prices. The framework combines six unsupervised component risk models — a physics-based productionconsistency model, a transfer-pricing deviation model, a cost-inflation model, a royaltyintegrity model, a revenue-feasibility model, and a mass-balance reconciliation model — with graph-theoretic analysis of related-party networks, and fuses the evidence through either a weighted composite score or naive-Bayes log-odds pooling with sequential updating. We establish formal properties of the estimator, including boundedness, monotonicity, bounded outlier influence under robust normalisation, almost-sure posterior consistency of the sequential Bayesian fusion under an expected-evidence drift condition, and a closedform detection-power bound for single-channel misreporting under log-normal measurement noise. A simulation study on a synthetic panel of 600 firms observed over 12 quarters, with five injected fraud typologies at 20% prevalence, shows that MDRIA attains an AUC of 0.858 (composite) and 0.869 (Bayesian fusion) without any labelled training data, compared with 0.643 for an Isolation Forest applied to raw financial features. When MDRIA component scores are supplied as features to a supervised gradient-boosting classifier, AUC rises to 0.970 (CI 0.95–0.99), exceeding all purely data-driven baselines in the study. Under the simulated conditions, evaders who spread small distortions across several reporting channels — the strategy most resistant to single-indicator audit rules — are the most detectable under joint-consistency testing (AUC 1.000). We discuss deployment architecture, explainability, data requirements, and policy implications for revenue authorities, supreme audit institutions, and international organisations supporting domestic resource mobilisation. ices, royalties, and shipments are jointly feasible given engineering identities, geological constraints, statutory rules, and market reference prices. Six unsupervised, individually interpretable risk components—physics, transfer-pricing, cost-inflation, royalty-integrity, revenue-feasibility, and mass-balance—are fused by weighted composite or sequential Bayesian log-odds pooling, with proven boundedness, robustness, posterior consistency, and detection-power bounds. On a synthetic 600-firm panel, label-free MDRIA reaches AUC 0.87 (vs. 0.64 for Isolation Forest); multi-channel "spread-thin" evasion is its most detectable typology (AUC 1.000). Includes deployment architecture, explainability, and policy implications for revenue authorities and international organisations.

For more research visit my Website.

title: Can a Religious Message Increase Forest Conservation? Evidence from Forest users in Burundi
affiliations: University of Burundi, University of Burundi and Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences

detail.title: Can a Religious Message Increase Forest Conservation? Evidence from Forest users in Burundi
detail.abstract: We study whether religious messaging can help address an environmental collective-action problem. We conduct a field experiment among forest users in rural Burundi, who are randomly assigned to hear a religious stewardship message, a secular civic-duty message, or a neutral message before deciding how much to contribute to forest conservation in a public-goods game. With 80% probability, the amount placed in the conservation account is donated to the public office responsible for forest protection. We find that the religious message increases contributions by 2.7 percentage points relative to the neutral message. This effect is statistically significant at the 5% level and corresponds to a 12.27% increase. The secular message has a smaller and statistically insignificant effect of 0.8 percentage points relative to the neutral message. The difference between the effects of the religious and secular messages is 1.8 percentage points, but is not statistically significant. We find no evidence that treatment effects vary with religiosity, religious affiliation, dependence on forest income, prior exposure to environmental messages in church, or pro-environmental perceptions. Our results suggest that religion can strengthen environmental cooperation by increasing individuals' willingness to bear private costs for conservation, even among those whose livelihoods depend directly on forest resources.

title: Optimal Taker Delays in In-Play Event Contract Markets

detail.title: Optimal Taker Delays in In-Play Event Contract Markets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author trades on venues discussed in this paper, including Polymarket, and therefore has a financial interest in the market-design outcomes analysed. The paper uses no proprietary or non-public information from any venue. The author has received no funding, data or other consideration from any exchange, betting operator or market-making firm.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study involves no human participants, no animal subjects and no personal data. It is a theoretical model calibrated to publicly available institutional parameters.
declarations.funderStatement: None. This research received no funding from any public, commercial or not-for-profit source.

detail.abstract: Between December 2025 and mid-2026 every major event-contract venue adopted a taker delay on in-play sports markets. The market-design literature these venues implicitly invoke was built for equity markets, where the speed advantage snipers exploit is purchased and therefore unbounded. In in-play sports markets it is neither: the advantage is the broadcast lag between the stadium and the exchange, measured in seconds, set by television infrastructure and unavailable at any price. I show this makes the taker delay a threshold instrument rather than a marginal one, and derive seven results. First, a delay protects a quote only when it exceeds the realized feed lag, so a delay below the shortest feed lag is strictly dominated by no delay at all. Second, the equilibrium spread schedule is a monotone transform of the feed-lag survival function, so an exchange's own quotes identify the lag distribution it faces. Third, and centrally, when sniper attendance is endogenous the total rent extracted by snipers equals exactly what uninformed traders overpay relative to the market maker's cost floor; this accounting identity implies the delay that deters entry is strictly shorter than the delay that wins every race, and it is decreasing in book depth-deeper books are harder to protect. Fourth, the welfare-optimal delay is bang-bang. Fifth, exempting market makers by identity rather than by order type returns up to one hundred percent of the protection to the exempt class as rent. Sixth, because event contracts resolve to a bound, no admissible two-sided quote survives high resolution intensity, so withdrawal rather than spread-widening is the equilibrium response, binding first in contracts furthest from fifty cents. Seventh, when venues compete for uninformed order flow, imposing a delay is a dominant strategy whether or not it reduces adverse selection, because diverting snipers to a rival makes one's own book look cheaper; the delay-setting game is a prisoner's dilemma, which converts venue discretion into a case for coordination. Calibrating to published Betfair delay schedules, the delays currently deployed on football and basketball fall below the support of the feed-lag distribution and are predicted to reduce spreads by nothing. The protection they could deliver is worth 0.35 of a minimum tick in football open play but 15.5 ticks in the seconds around a shot, which implies that state-contingency, not duration, is the design margin that matters.

title: Guerreiro Ramos and Sociological Reduction: Dilemmas and Prospects for Brazilian Economic Development

detail.title: Guerreiro Ramos and Sociological Reduction: Dilemmas and Prospects for Brazilian Economic Development
detail.abstract: This   article   examines   Alberto   Guerreiro   Ramos’s  contributions  to  understanding  the  dilemmas  and  prospects  of  Brazilian  economic  development,  em-phasizing  the  originality  and  relevance  of  his  thought.  The methodological approach is based on a bibliographic review, aiming to identifying the State of the Art on the subject.  The  analysis  is  structured  around  four  axes:  i)   biographical   context,   ii)   theoretical-methodological   foundations,  iii)  critiques  of  structural  obstacles,  and  iv)  proposals  for  a  national-developmental  project  in  Brazil.  The  study  concludes  that  Guerreiro  Ramos’s  work  rep-resents a landmark in Critical Sociology and Sociology of Development, in Brazil and should be further explored in contemporary economic studies.

reference: Journal of Latin American Sciences and Culture, volume 8, issue 12, 2026[10.52428/27888991.v8i12.1537]
title: Green Skills and Graduate Employability in Hospitality Vocational Education: Evidence from Ghana
affiliations: , University of Ghana - University of Ghana Business School (UGBS) and University of Ghana - University of Ghana Business School (UGBS)

detail.title: Green Skills and Graduate Employability in Hospitality Vocational Education: Evidence from Ghana

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Latin American Sciences and Culture, volume 8, issue 12, 2026[10.52428/27888991.v8i12.1537]

detail.abstract: Ghana's hospitality sector faces a persistent unemployment skills gap, with graduates from technical and vocational education and training (TVET) institutions experiencing challenges in acquiring the green competencies increasingly demanded by a sustainabilityoriented labour market. This study examined the relationship between green skills training, green competency acquisition, and graduate employability within Ghana's hospitality TVET sector, positioning green competency acquisition as a mediating mechanism. Guided by Human Capital Theory and Social Learning Theory, the study adopted a quantitative research approach. Data were collected through a threestage process: (i) purposive selection of accredited TVET institutions; (ii) proportionate stratified random sampling yielding 346 final-year hospitality students from mainstream universities, technical universities, and TVET-designated Colleges of Education; and (iii) administration of a pilot-tested, structured self-administered questionnaire, adapted from established green training and graduate employability instruments. Data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) through SmartPLS, involving measurement model assessment, structural model evaluation, and mediation analysis using bootstrapping procedures. The findings indicate that green skills training significantly and positively influences green competency acquisition (β = 0.757, p < 0.001, R² = 0.573). Green competency acquisition also significantly predicts graduate employability (β = 0.665, p < 0.001, R² = 0.463). Furthermore, green competency acquisition partially mediates the relationship between green skills training and graduate employability (indirect β = 0.379, 95% CI, 0.288, 0.471), demonstrating that competency development represents a key pathway through which green training enhances perceived labour market readiness. The study contributes empirical evidence from a developing-country TVET context by demonstrating the importance of integrating green skills development into hospitality education. The findings highlight the need for curriculum reform, national green competency frameworks, and stronger collaboration between TVET institutions and industry to improve sustainable workforce development.

title:
Empirical Evaluation of the Agentic Reputation Substrate 
Deliberation, the Composition of Error, and the Registered Measurement of Agency Costs in a Controlled Multi-Model Cohort
affiliations: University of St. Thomas - School of Law (Minnesota)

detail.title:
Empirical Evaluation of the Agentic Reputation Substrate 
Deliberation, the Composition of Error, and the Registered Measurement of Agency Costs in a Controlled Multi-Model Cohort
detail.abstract: Multi-agent systems built from large language models inherit the oldest problem in the economic theory of organization: the divergence between what an agent does and what the principal can observe, verify, and price. The empirical literature on LLM agent collaboration measures capability under incentive-free conditions, and its benchmarks accordingly cannot distinguish an agent population that performs well because it is capable from one that performs well because it is aligned. This Article reports a completed, preregistered discovery-to-confirmation cycle on an institutional treatment within a working agent economy. The instrument is the agentic reputation substrate, a coordination architecture that subjects work and validation to reputation-bearing accountability. The treatment reported here is a structured deliberation layer, varied against a matched non-deliberative control within a controlled multi-model cohort. The discovery campaign returned a null on its registered primary endpoint, net discrimination (Youden's J +0.0250, 95% CI [-0.0502, +0.0985]), and two exploratory effects: deliberation reduced over-approval (pooled -0.1336) and reduced unanimity (pooled -0.1992). The program then preregistered a fresh confirmatory campaign before any confirmatory computation. Both primary hypotheses confirmed under the preregistered rule: over-approval -0.1610 (95% CI [-0.2091, -0.1128]) and unanimity -0.2542 (95% CI [-0.2984, -0.2091]), with the randomization audit and preregistered data-quality gate passing. Net discrimination remained null (+0.0606, CI crossing zero), as preregistered. The finding is a composition result: agent deliberation does not measurably improve net discrimination. Agent deliberation changes which errors validation pools make, reducing approval of work rejected by ground truth and reducing unanimous consensus, a pattern consistent with disruption of an informational cascade. The Article retains the nine-metric agency-cost battery as a registered forward program and offers the discovery-to-confirmation cycle as a methodological template for empirical claims about agent economies.

title: Shallow Greening: Financial Frictions and the Composition of Compliance
affiliations: The University of Melbourne and Xiamen University Malaysia Campus - School of Economics and Management

detail.title: Shallow Greening: Financial Frictions and the Composition of Compliance
detail.abstract: An emission price can induce remedial end-of-pipe abatement, which removes emissions after generation, or process innovation, which permanently reduces them at the source. We study how financial frictions shape this choice. Using U.S. firm-level data, we show that compliance follows a financing-based ladder: firms use end-of-pipe abatement first and add innovation as net worth rises. We rationalize this evidence by developing a tractable three-period model in which end-of-pipe capital is pledgeable and financed period by period, whereas innovation is more cost-effective but requires up-front, non-pledgeable funding. It generates a compliance pecking order, from no abatement to remediation to process innovation as net worth rises. The intermediate regime, shallow greening, comprises firms that comply without transforming production. End-of-pipe abatement creates a residual-base channel that can crowd out process innovation by shrinking the emissions it can save. An infinite-horizon model with heterogeneous firms, entry and exit, and a ratchet ladder of emission intensity provides a framework for quantifying aggregate implications. The three-period policy analysis shows that emission prices and asset-based green credit can buy remediation without promoting transformation, whereas net-worth support and green-innovation subsidies promote transition.

title: Beyond Extraction: Governing Sustainable Mining, Resource Justice, and Community Resilience in Turkana County, Kenya

detail.title: Beyond Extraction: Governing Sustainable Mining, Resource Justice, and Community Resilience in Turkana County, Kenya
detail.abstract: Turkana County, in Kenya's arid north, sits atop two extractive frontiers that are advancing far ahead of the institutions meant to govern them: artisanal gold mining at Lomeguro/Naduat, Locheremoit, Kalomwae, and Moruongor, and the commercial oil development now proceeding in the South Lokichar Basin of Turkana East and South. This paper synthesises publicly available government, media, county, and academic sources to examine the governance gap that has accompanied this dual extractive economy and the socioeconomic , environmental, and security consequences that follow from it. Drawing on resource curse theory, common-pool resource governance, devolution and subsidiarity theory, and environmental justice frameworks, the paper documents recurring patterns across the mining sites: fatal shaft collapses linked to the absence of appropriate equipment and safety standards, unregulated mineral pricing and trading, weak county revenue and royalty capture, contested land governance around conservancies, and infrastructural, educational, and social strains on host communities. It situates Turkana's experience within comparative artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) formalisation literature from Ghana and Tanzania, and within Kenya's own Mining Act, 2016 and its devolved royalty-sharing architecture. The paper's principal contribution is the Integrated Sustainable Mining Governance Framework (ISMGF), a ten-pillar model linking governance, environmental sustainability, community well-being, economic inclusion, security, technology, local content, transparency, climate resilience, and intergenerational equity. The paper concludes with a set of practical, sequenced policy recommendations for the Turkana County Government, the national government, and development partners, including a proposed Turkana Artisanal Mining Authority, designated mineral trading centres, a county mineral cadastre, and an environmental restoration fund financed throughproduction levies.

title: Housing Price Prediction in Ireland: A Machine Learning Framework Integrating Geospatial Encodings and Macroeconomic Indicators

detail.title: Housing Price Prediction in Ireland: A Machine Learning Framework Integrating Geospatial Encodings and Macroeconomic Indicators

No human participants were involved in the research. No personally identifiable information was collected or processed. Formal ethics approval was not required.
