detail.title: The Liquidity Paradox: Does Fintech Integration Fuel Impulse Spending or Financial Literacy among Gig Workers?
detail.abstract: India's gig economy has expanded rapidly, and fintech innovations such as instant payouts and digital wallets now give workers near-immediate access to their earnings. Yet easier access to income does not automatically translate into financial well-being. Drawing on primary survey data from 244 gig workers across Delhi NCR, Mumbai, and Bengaluru, this study finds that while 66.4% actively use instant payouts, 70.9% save rarely or never, only 13.9% can meet a ₹10,000 emergency independently, and 56.6% lack health insurance. Awareness of PMJJBY remains low (59.0% unaware; 8.6% enrolled). Digital access has improved convenience but not financial security.

title: Can You Trust the Graph Beneath the Agent? A Reliability Metrology for Enterprise Skills Graphs: The FACTS Dimensions and the Skills Graph Reliability Index

detail.title: Can You Trust the Graph Beneath the Agent? A Reliability Metrology for Enterprise Skills Graphs: The FACTS Dimensions and the Skills Graph Reliability Index

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known financial, professional, personal, or commercial conflicts of interest that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this manuscript. The views expressed in this paper are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the views, policies, or positions of the author's employer.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This article is a conceptual and normative research work intended to stimulate discussion on the classification, governance, and responsible deployment of AI-enabled workforce intelligence systems. No human subjects, proprietary datasets, or confidential organizational information were used.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this article.

detail.abstract:
Enterprise skills graphs, which connect skills to the people who hold them and the work that requires them, have become the data substrate on which agentic HR systems recommend hiring, mobility, reskilling, and redeployment. A consensus has formed among HR analysts that the value of these systems depends less on the sophistication of the agents than on the trustworthiness of the graph beneath them. That trustworthiness, however, is discussed almost entirely in qualitative terms. Where it is quantified at all, it is reduced to a single proxy: coverage, the percentage of roles or people for which some skill data exists. Coverage answers how much data an organisation holds. It is silent on whether that data can be trusted enough to let an autonomous agent act.
This paper develops the missing measurement science. Working within a design-science method and drawing on established data-quality standards (ISO/IEC 25012, ISO 8000, the FAIR principles) and on machine-learning calibration theory, it defines a reliability construct for skills graphs along five dimensions: Freshness, Accuracy of stated confidence, Contestability, Traceability, and Stability, which form the mnemonic FACTS. The dimensions are derived from the conditions under which an automated decision is defensible rather than assembled as a list, and each is operationalised as a metric computable on a graph's nodes and edges. They are combined into a dashboard-ready Skills Graph Reliability Index (SGRI) through a gated, deny-overrides aggregation rather than a weighted mean, so that weakness on any one dimension cannot be concealed by strength on another. SGRI resolves to three decision bands: act, human-gate, or do not automate.
The paper makes five contributions. To begin with, it argues that unreliability in a skills graph compound rather than averages out under agentic use, because agent inferences written back without provenance contaminate the evidence against which later inferences would be validated, a mechanism named here evidential circularity. Second, it demonstrates that mechanism computationally. In a simulation of 20,000 edges over twelve cycles, unlabelled write-back caused measured calibration error to improve while true calibration error degraded, and the divergence increased with the writeback rate. At a write-back rate of 0.50 the contaminated graph reported a lower calibration error than a fully labelled control while its true error was approximately 4.8 times worse, so an organisation comparing the two on measured calibration would have preferred the corrupted graph. Third, the paper specifies the SGRI aggregation and decision bands and defends the deny-overrides rule on grounds of asymmetric loss. Fourth, it states the boundary of the construct explicitly: SGRI measures the trustworthiness of the evidence base, not the quality of inference drawn from it. Fifth, it confronts the ground-truth problem, since calibration in this domain depends on an oracle that is itself biased, and proposes triangulation and mandatory oracle-provenance disclosure as partial remedies. Fairness is treated as a stratification requirement across all five dimensions rather than as a sixth dimension. A reference architecture, a worked illustration, and a set of falsifiable propositions complete the paper. No claim is made that the index predicts decision quality; that relationship is stated as a falsifiable proposition and remains untested.

title: The Dynamics of Redemption: From Sovereign Decree, Intercession, Compassion, Justice, Calling, Leading, and the Centripetal Rest of Grace-A Chiastic Exegetical and Doctrinal Study of Genesis 18:20-19:38

detail.title: The Dynamics of Redemption: From Sovereign Decree, Intercession, Compassion, Justice, Calling, Leading, and the Centripetal Rest of Grace-A Chiastic Exegetical and Doctrinal Study of Genesis 18:20-19:38
detail.abstract: Genesis 18:20–19:38 records the complete narrative of the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah and the redemption of Lot. Throughout the history of interpretation, exegetes have usually read the passage in linear sequence, treating it either as a case study in the theology of judgment or as a moral exhortation. This study argues that the passage is in fact arranged as a thirteen-part concentric chiastic structure (A–B–C–D–E–F–X–F′–E′– D′–C′–B′–A′), pivoting on Genesis 19:16: “Because the LORD was merciful to Lot, the two men seized his hand … and brought them out.” The literary design itself thus communicates a profound theology of redemption: the true theological center of the passage is sovereignty alone, grace alone, and irresistible grace, rather than Lot’s personal virtue or moral choice. This study first surveys premodern and modern exegetical literature on the passage and identifies unresolved questions. It then offers a unit-by-unit exposition of the chiastic structure, examining the exegetical content of the six corresponding pairs, the logical relationship between each pair, and the theological relation of each pair to the central axis. Special attention is given to the Christological significance of the center (19:16): the LORD himself “seizes,” “has mercy upon,” and “brings out” a sinner who lingers and refuses to leave, prefiguring the New Testament declarations that “the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost” (Luke 19:10) and that “God, being rich in mercy, because of the great love with which he loved us … made us alive together with Christ” (Eph. 2:4–5). On this basis, the study proceeds to develop a systematic doctrinal synthesis, pastoral application, and dialogue with the history of interpretation.

title: The Missing Constraint in Cybernetics: Meta-Capacity as a Prerequisite for Adaptation

detail.title: The Missing Constraint in Cybernetics: Meta-Capacity as a Prerequisite for Adaptation
detail.abstract:
Purpose 

 This paper examines a theoretical limitation in current cybernetic approaches concerning the conditions that enable complex systems to sustain development under increasing complexity. While cybernetics has extensively studied regulation, feedback, viability, and adaptation, less attention has been given to why some systems maintain developmental trajectories while others become increasingly dependent on adaptive or compensatory responses.

Design/methodology/approach

 The paper develops a conceptual analysis based on the Meta-Capacity framework and positions it within established cybernetic perspectives, including requisite variety, organisational cybernetics, and complex adaptive systems theory. The study differentiates between development, adaptation, and compensation as distinct systemic processes and proposes a conceptual model of their dynamic relationship. 

Findings 

 The analysis proposes that development represents the normal trajectory of a viable complex system, while adaptation emerges when developmental continuity is interrupted. Compensation is interpreted as a subsequent response when adaptation cannot restore developmental continuity. The framework further proposes that recurrent compensation may generate a Compensatory Pendulum, in which repeated corrective responses temporarily reduce systemic tension while creating conditions for subsequent compensation.

Originality/value

 The paper introduces Meta-Capacity as an analytical construct describing the accessibility of developmental potential and explaining why systems with comparable structures and resources may exhibit different trajectories. The framework complements existing cybernetic theory by identifying accessibility as a previously underexplored condition of regulation, viability, and adaptation. The proposed relationships provide a basis for future empirical operationalization and testing across complex systems.

title: The Probability Distribution of a Put Option
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: The Probability Distribution of a Put Option
detail.abstract: This paper derives the probability law of the discounted payoff of a European put option, extending the framework previously developed for European calls using the generalized transformation formula for random variables. By treating the payoff itself as a random variable, and by including the discount factor directly in the payoff transformation, we obtain closed-form expressions for its probability density and cumulative distribution under Geometric Brownian Motion. We then state the transformation for an arbitrary admissible distribution of the underlying asset. The resulting put distribution mirrors that of the call, while reflecting the defining asymmetry of the contract: the payoff has an atom at the origin and is bounded above by its discounted strike price. The lognormal case is developed explicitly, while the same functional representation provides the basis for extending the framework to broader admissible distributions of the underlying.

title: The Impact of Multi-Selection in Ride-Hailing Platforms
affiliations: INSEAD and

detail.title: The Impact of Multi-Selection in Ride-Hailing Platforms
detail.abstract: Ride-hailing platforms offer vertically differentiated service products (e.g., standard vs. premium), where riders traditionally select exactly one option per trip request (single-selection). A growing number of platforms such as Grab and DiDi now introduce a multi-selection feature that allows riders to simultaneously indicate willingness for multiple service tiers, with the platform determining the final assignment. We study how optimal pricing and allocation policies should be designed under multi-selection, how they differ from the single-selection benchmark, and whether the additional flexibility can improve profitability without degrading customer welfare. Methodology/results: We develop a steady-state queueing model with price-and delay-sensitive riders and earnings-sensitive drivers. Under the single-selection benchmark, we characterize how vertical differentiation and endogenous congestion jointly shape optimal pricing and cross-tier substitution effects. Under multi-selection, we introduce an α-allocation policy governing how the platform routes mixed-demand riders across tiers. We show that optimal pricing is tightly coupled with the allocation rule, giving rise to two distinct configurations (premium-screening and premium-accommodation), under which pricing responses to service quality improvements differ qualitatively from the single-selection benchmark. To compare the two regimes, we impose a customer welfare constraint ensuring that multiselection does not exploit riders' flexibility. We find that multi-selection can achieve a "win-win" outcome weakly improving both profitability and welfare, but only under specific conditions on service quality differentiation, demand intensity, supply capacity distribution, and delay sensitivity. When these conditions fail, single-selection can be more profitable despite multi-selection's additional flexibility. Managerial implications: Our results suggest that pricing and allocation must be coordinated under multi-selection, with the pricing posture adjusted in tandem with how mixed demand is routed across tiers. More broadly, the choice between single-selection and multi-selection can itself serve as a managerial lever: since multi-selection is implemented at the user-interface level, platforms can switch between regimes in response to evolving operational conditions, balancing profitability with long-term customer trust.

title: Navigating Global Sourcing Shocks: The Value of Strategic Abandonment and Responsive Pricing
affiliations: School of Business Administration, South China University of Technology, School of Business Administration South China University of  Technology and Hong Kong Polytechnic University - Department of Logistics and Maritime Studies

detail.title: Navigating Global Sourcing Shocks: The Value of Strategic Abandonment and Responsive Pricing
detail.abstract: Problem definition: Random shocks happen frequently in global sourcing, leading to rising transportation costs and uncertain delays that induce demand loss. To navigate sourcing shocks, we observe that some firms strategically abandon goods to reduce supply, whereas others further adopt responsive pricing to better utilize supply. While responsive pricing has been extensively studied in the literature, strategic abandonment, and its interactions with responsive pricing, have received little attention in prior studies. Methodology/results: We develop a multi-stage game-theoretic model to investigate the effects of strategic abandonment on product demand, effective supply, and consumer surplus under global sourcing shocks, and characterize how these effects are further influenced by responsive pricing. By structuring our analysis into two regimes, without strategic abandonment and with strategic abandonment, we first reveal the value of strategic abandonment and outline its activation conditions: a high transportation cost escalation encourages strategic abandonment, while a high risk probability discourages it. We further show that adopting responsive pricing may undermine the value of strategic abandonment, implying that the two mechanisms may act as either complements or substitutes. Finally, we identify conditions under which strategic abandonment combined with responsive pricing can achieve a Pareto improvement for both supply chain members and consumer surplus. Managerial implications: Our analysis provides a better understanding of how strategic abandonment mitigates the impact of sourcing shocks and reminds global firm managers that using both strategic abandonment and responsive pricing blindly can be very detrimental. An effective sourcing risk mitigation mechanism must be carefully designed by evaluating the value of contingency strategies in the face of supply chain uncertainty.

title: Joint Admission and Service Rate Control in Service Systems with Heterogeneous Customers
affiliations: Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) - Department of Information Systems, Business Statistics and Operations Management, Sun Yat-sen University,  and Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) - Department of Information Systems, Business Statistics and Operations Management

detail.title: Joint Admission and Service Rate Control in Service Systems with Heterogeneous Customers
detail.abstract: Many capacity-constrained service systems can manage congestion through two levers at once: whether to admit an arriving customer, and whether to accelerate service at a cost. In this paper, we study the joint optimization of both decisions in a finite-capacity loss system with heterogeneous arrivals. The admission is governed by a state-dependent threshold on rejection cost and acceleration is a binary speed-up decision incurring an occupancy-proportional cost. We formulate the problem as a continuous-time Markov decision process and show that the optimal stationary policy has a double-threshold structure: the admission threshold is non-decreasing in the occupancy level, and the accelerated service rate is only used when the occupancy is sufficiently high. We further derive a closed-form solution for the single-server case and demonstrate how the two decisions interact with each other. Numerical experiments show that jointly optimizing the service-rate and admission decisions, compared with optimizing the admission decision alone, substantially reduces system long-run cost. In addition, it leads to smaller occupancy variation due to twosided balancing. The results indicate that admission and service-rate control should be planned jointly when managing service systems.

This paper examines the constitutional and legal dimensions of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in India. It discusses its historical background, constitutional framework, judicial interpretation, and its impact on equality, gender justice, and national integration. title: Roles of Personality and Positionality in Developing the Leadership Characteristics of Female Construction Professionals
affiliations: , Obafemi Awolowo University, Obafemi Awolowo University, Obafemi Awolowo University, Obafemi Awolowo University and Obafemi Awolowo University

detail.title: Roles of Personality and Positionality in Developing the Leadership Characteristics of Female Construction Professionals

keywords: Under-Representation of Women in Leadership Positions

detail.abstract: Gender inequality continues to limit women's advancement into leadership positions in the construction industry. Understanding the factors that shape women's leadership development is therefore important for improving gender equity in the sector. This study examined the influence of personality and positionality on the leadership advancement of female construction professionals and their development of leadership characteristics. The study was informed by Trait Theory of Leadership, Adler's Birth Order Theory, and the Big Five Personality Theory. Data collected from female construction professionals were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The findings indicate that personality and positionality significantly influence women's leadership advancement and can strengthen their participation in construction leadership. The study also found that challenging conventional gender norms can support women's progression into leadership positions. These findings suggest that leadership development initiatives should account for individual personality characteristics and the positional contexts within which women work. Construction organizations can use such initiatives to identify and develop leadership potential, address barriers affecting women's progression, strengthen leadership competencies, and create more equitable pathways to leadership. The study contributes to the understanding of how individual characteristics and workplace positionality shape women's leadership advancement in construction. It also provides a basis for developing targeted leadership development strategies that support women's career progression and enable construction organizations to benefit from a more diverse and capable leadership workforce.

title: Crisis Management Strategies and Organizational Challenges in the Construction Industry: A Structured Review with Practitioner Insights

detail.title: Crisis Management Strategies and Organizational Challenges in the Construction Industry: A Structured Review with Practitioner Insights

keywords: Generating response Copilot said: Crisis Management

detail.abstract: Crisis management in construction is frequently studied through the lens of individual leadership competencies, yet the strategic frameworks and organizational-level obstacles that shape how a construction firm responds to disruption receive comparatively less structured attention. This paper synthesises a structured literature review with practitioner interview data to examine how crisis management is conceptualised, structured, and obstructed within construction organisations. The review identifies three staged models used to describe crisis management in construction, prediction, prevention and preparedness, control, and learning and recovery, and five distinct strategic approaches: escape, solution, proactive, reactive, and interactive. Nine semi-structured interviews with German construction professionals were then used to examine which of these challenges are most acutely experienced in practice. Financial volatility linked to global economic fluctuation, communication breakdown across stakeholder groups, and a shortage of structured technical and managerial training emerged as the three most consistently reported organizational obstacles. The paper argues that an interactive strategic approach, one that treats crisis assessment as continuous across the pre-crisis, response, and recovery stages rather than confined to any single phase, offers the most complete account of how resilient construction organisations actually operate, and that current practice remains constrained less by a lack of strategic frameworks than by the organizational conditions, communication infrastructure, and workforce training needed to execute them.

title: Development and Validation of a Competency Assessment Model for Study Abroad Students

detail.title: Development and Validation of a Competency Assessment Model for Study Abroad Students
detail.abstract: Although study abroad programs have proliferated across higher education, the field lacks a psychometrically rigorous instrument for measuring the intercultural competence that such programs are designed to foster (Bettez & Lineberry, 2020; Schartner, 2015). Existing measures rely predominantly on self-report methods as the one proposed here. Even if this approach could be vulnerable to social desirability bias, ceiling effects, and persistent construct ambiguity, which has led to inconsistent interpretations of student development across programs (Griffith et al., 2016; Jaiswal et al., 2024; Stemler et al., 2014), this paper addresses that gap by proposing a situational personal judgment test to assess the cognitive, affective, and behavioral dimensions of intercultural competencies among outbound study abroad students (Allen, 2022; Schembri, 2024). The paper articulates the theoretical rationale for the proposed target construct, details the design specifications and item development procedures, and outlines the framework for collecting validity and reliability evidence in accordance with contemporary standards in educational and psychological measurement (Griffith et al., 2016; Ji, 2020; Sercu, 2004). By formalizing observable indicators of intercultural performance, the resulting instrument is intended to provide researchers, program administrators, and accreditation reviewers with actionable, longitudinal evidence of student development during and following international immersion (Cartwright et al., 2021; Hanada, 2019; Shadowen et al., 2015). Conclusion state the multidimensionality of global competency is verified, proving that students develop distinct cognitive, affective, and social-emotional profiles that must be scored, evaluated, and fostered independently rather than collapsed into a generic score. The Global Competency Assessment Framework (GCAF), represents a highly reliable, error-minimized, and psychometrically distinct diagnostic battery.

title: Identifying Inventory Policies from Digital Traces: A Data-Driven Approach Using Real-World Order Patterns
affiliations: Kuehne Logistics University and Kuehne Logistics University

detail.title: Identifying Inventory Policies from Digital Traces: A Data-Driven Approach Using Real-World Order Patterns
detail.abstract: Understanding how inventory policies are implemented in practice remains a fundamental challenge in operations management because replenishment rules are rarely shared with others. However, different inventory policies leave identifiable signatures in transactional order data, creating an opportunity to infer otherwise hidden replenishment structures. This study develops a two-stage data-driven framework for identifying inventory policies directly from observed order behavior. In the first stage, semi-synthetic data, machine-learning classification, and expert evaluation are used to develop and validate a robust policy-identification model. In the second stage, the selected model is applied to a large-scale order dataset provided by a global travel-retail wholesaler, comprising 128,834 order time series across a diverse set of retailers and product categories. The results reveal only partial alignment between observed replenishment behavior and classical inventory-theory expectations. While policy selection varies systematically with product characteristics, substantial heterogeneity exists across retailers, and identical products are frequently managed using different replenishment rules. Retailer-level factors explain more variation in inferred policy behavior than product characteristics alone, highlighting the importance of organizational context in inventory-policy implementation. The study contributes a scalable methodology for inventory-policy identification and provides large-scale empirical evidence on how inventory policies are implemented in practice. More broadly, it demonstrates how the digital traces embedded in transactional order data can be used to uncover otherwise unobservable operational decision structures.

title: An Analysis of Japan's Robo-Advisor Market: Changes since the Introduction of the New NISA System and Implications for the Korean Market
affiliations: Mirae Asset Global Investment

detail.title: An Analysis of Japan's Robo-Advisor Market: Changes since the Introduction of the New NISA System and Implications for the Korean Market
detail.abstract: This study analyzes Japan's robo-advisor industry, which has grown rapidly through partnerships and acquisitions with major financial institutions following the implementation of the new NISA (Nippon Individual Savings Account) system. The paper aims to identify the growth drivers of the industry by examining the impact of institutional changes-particularly the new NISA-on industry structure, as well as the linkage between the robo-advisor industry and the ETF market, and to draw policy implications for Korea's capital market. Japan's Financial Services Agency (FSA) has established a regulatory framework and investor protection standards for robo-advisors, laying the groundwork for trust in digital asset management services. Meanwhile, the expansion and permanent extension of the new NISA's tax-exemption limits have encouraged longterm, diversified investment among individual investors, which appears to have had a positive effect on the growth of the ETFbased robo-advisor market. Japan's experience offers important policy implications for Korea in building a digital-based longterm investment platform and a tax-linked asset management ecosystem. Drawing on Japan's growth experience, this study proposes three strategic directions for revitalizing Korea's robo-advisor industry: (1) providing investment incentives through regulatory clarification and stronger tax linkages; (2) building a sustainable financial ecosystem through mergers and acquisitions between traditional financial institutions and fintech firms; and (3) expanding online-centered robo-advisor services into offline channels and promoting the development of ETF-based products to support this expansion, thereby creating business linkages and synergy.

title: The Value of Timely Risk Assessment in Subcontract Management: Mitigating Schedule Slippage and Cost Overruns in Complex EPC Projects

detail.title: The Value of Timely Risk Assessment in Subcontract Management: Mitigating Schedule Slippage and Cost Overruns in Complex EPC Projects

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No people or organizations are influenced by study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: No need for ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding.

detail.abstract: In modern Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) megaprojects, prime contractors routinely outsource significant portions of specialized site execution to third-party subcontractors. While subcontracting allows for capacity scaling and domain-specific expertise, it introduces profound interface risks, commercial friction, and operational dependencies. This paper investigates the empirical and procedural value of implementing timely-specifically proactive and iterative-risk assessments within subcontract management workflows. By evaluating risk exposure during preaward, mobilization, execution, and closeout phases, project management teams can convert reactive dispute management into deterministic project control. Furthermore, this study introduces an operational framework for early warning risk identification, demonstrating that early intervention yields exponential cost and schedule savings compared to late-stage commercial claims and recovery efforts.

title: Forecasting Retail Sales Performance of Customer Shopping with Deep Learning-Based Predictive Analytics
affiliations: US Bank, Vanguard, Data Engineer Specialist, Microsoft Corp., Microsoft Corp., Microsoft Corporation and Ally Financial (Ally Financial Inc.)

detail.title: Forecasting Retail Sales Performance of Customer Shopping with Deep Learning-Based Predictive Analytics
detail.abstract: The effective management of inventories, demand planning, and strategic decisions of retail sales rely on the accurate forecasting of these activities. Conventional statistical and machine learning (ML) models are often not able to capture complex time dependencies and sequential trends in sales data, which increase prediction error. In this paper, the authors approach these issues by creating a deep learning-based predictive analytics model that is based on Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) model. The aim is to accurately forecast future sales going by the previous patterns, reducing errors in forecasting sales and giving practical information to retailers. Pre-processing, scaling, splitting, training, testing, deep learning (DL) model construction with hyperparameter tuning, and final model validation using Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and R-squared (R2) were applied to the retail sales data. Using the Adam optimizer and MSE loss function, the bi-LSTM model-which has two LSTM layers, dropout, and fully linked layers-was trained using GPU acceleration. The model performed well in prediction with MSE of 16.98, RMSE of 41.22, MAE of 26.38, MAPE of 23.27% and R ² of 0.9568 which was better than the currently used variants of Multilayer perceptron (MLP), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Linear Regression (LR) and Support Vector Regression (SVR). These findings validate that Bi-LSTM model is an effective tool to capture sales trends over time, to offer valid and practical prediction of customer shopping behaviour.

title: A Meeting Doesn't Need to Meet: Meetings Are for Alignment, Not Attendance
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: A Meeting Doesn't Need to Meet: Meetings Are for Alignment, Not Attendance
detail.abstract:
Meetings consume an increasing share of managerial time yet produce little: participants disengage, information is read aloud that could have been emailed, and decisions made in rooms are later rewritten in documents. The puzzle is not why meetings fail, but why organizations cannot stop holding failing meetings.

This paper proposes a meeting ontology. A meeting is a synchronous coordination event that generates alignment on at least one of four dimensions: Goal (what we aim to achieve), Object (what mechanism we operate on), Criteria (what standards define effective functioning), and Boundary (where the mechanism stops working). These four—GOCB—are minimal: a gathering that does not align on any of them is not a meeting in functional terms.

Without such an ontology, meeting research treats meetings as coordination, ritual, politics, bonding, or sensemaking—allowing any purpose to justify a meeting and eliminating criteria for necessity. This conceptual promiscuity enables meeting inflation.

Two decisive cases test the ontology. Peer review, the most complex and contested coordination system in science, operates almost entirely asynchronously—even under deliberate information barriers such as double-blind review—because GOCB is institutionalized in its structure. Parliaments also institutionalize GOCB but retain periodic meetings only as a pre‑digital legacy of required physical synchronization. If the highest‑stakes coordination systems can function with minimal or no synchronous meetings, then most organizational meetings that merely transmit information are not only inefficient—they are logically indefensible.

The implication is direct: a meeting that does not generate GOCB alignment is not performing its function and should be subject to justification. And if the world’s most demanding knowledge system runs on email, face‑to‑face presence is not a requirement—it is a default we have never questioned.

title: Proof Before Fielding: The Army Is Adopting Military AI Faster Than It Can Test It - Medicine Already Built the Fix

detail.title: Proof Before Fielding: The Army Is Adopting Military AI Faster Than It Can Test It - Medicine Already Built the Fix

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationships with other people or organizations that could have influenced, or be perceived to have influenced, this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This article is a policy analysis based on publicly available sources and involved no human participants, patient data, or case studies; no ethics approval or consent was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This work received no funding from any agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
In the first half of 2026, the United States committed itself, at the highest level and in writing, to putting artificial intelligence at the center of how it fights and how it decides. National Security Presidential Memorandum 11, the June 2026 executive order on advanced AI, and the Department of War's Artificial Intelligence Strategy all set a single tempo: adopt fast, remove barriers, field at wartime speed. The strategic logic is sound. The execution carries a defect that no amount of speed can outrun. The policy that mandates adoption did not bring with it a method for determining whether a fielded system actually improves decisions under the conditions of real operations. The Army is being told to become an AI-first force before it has an evaluation science capable of telling good AI from AI that merely accelerates error.

Commercial benchmarking cannot close this gap. Benchmarks score models on static question sets under clean conditions. War happens under uncertainty, deception, jamming, and time pressure. A model can win a leaderboard and still collapse in the field. One publicly reported data point captures the problem. A fielded targeting aid reportedly identified armor correctly about sixty percent of the time in clear weather and about thirty percent in snow, while human analysts in the same reporting were correct about eighty-four percent of the time. A benchmark run in good weather would have certified a system that halves in the conditions under which wars are often fought, and that in one reported comparison performed below the humans it was meant to help.

This article makes a claim that is narrow and, I argue, correct. The evaluation science the force needs already exists, in clinical epidemiology, and it should be adapted rather than reinvented at wartime speed. Medicine spent a century building a machinery for exactly this situation: high consequence decisions, irreducible uncertainty, powerful incentives to overclaim, and a body count when evaluation fails. Six components of that machinery transfer directly to military AI test and evaluation. Uplift studies are randomized controlled trials. Automation bias is a confounder that inflates apparent performance and must be measured and controlled. 

Demonstrations without statistical power prove nothing. External validity is the discipline of asking whether a result generalizes to the theater where it will be used. Pre-registration of metrics and thresholds is the antidote to selecting a flattering number after the fact. Failure-mode surveillance is pharmacovigilance for fielded models. Together these describe a phased evaluation pipeline analogous to clinical trial phases, from controlled feasibility testing to operational effectiveness to continuous post-fielding surveillance.

reference: The Lumbini Journal of Business and Economics, volume 11, issue 1, 2023[10.3126/ljbe.v11i1.54337]
title: Beyond Hardware: Barriers to ICT Integration Among Secondary-Level Teachers in Gulmi, Nepal: A Descriptive Mixed-Source Study

detail.title: Beyond Hardware: Barriers to ICT Integration Among Secondary-Level Teachers in Gulmi, Nepal: A Descriptive Mixed-Source Study

publicationDetails.detailsText: The Lumbini Journal of Business and Economics, volume 11, issue 1, 2023[10.3126/ljbe.v11i1.54337]

detail.abstract: This study examined barriers to information and communication technology (ICT) integration among secondary-level teachers in community schools of Gulmi District, Nepal. A crosssectional descriptive mixed-source design combined a multiple-response teacher checklist completed by 44 purposively selected teachers from 11 community secondary schools with aggregated classroom-observation evidence. Because four teachers were purposively selected from each school regardless of school size, the sample was non-proportionate; the results therefore describe the participating teachers and should not be interpreted as district-wide prevalence estimates. Frequencies and percentages were treated as descriptive indicators rather than scale scores. Insufficient ICT skills and knowledge and inadequate school equipment were each reported by all participants (100%). Lack of teacher training and limited administrative support were each reported by 95.5%. A compound checklist item combining unstable electricity with inadequate facilities and resources was also endorsed by 95.5%; its components cannot be interpreted separately. Limited preparation time was reported by 90.9%, lack of technical assistance by 86.4%, and unreliable internet and weak curriculum alignment by 77.3% each. Low confidence (38.6%) and low motivation (34.1%) were reported less often than structural and capability constraints. Observations indicated limited device access, interruptions caused by power, connectivity, and equipment failure, uneven teacher competence, and reliance on presentations, videos, and online resources rather than interactive applications. Student interest and participation appeared greater when ICT was used purposefully, although learning outcomes were not measured. The findings indicate that sustainable ICT integration requires coordinated attention to functional infrastructure, teacher development, preparation time, technical support, curriculum guidance, school leadership, and implementation monitoring.

title: Flags in Relation
affiliations: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey - Rutgers Law School

detail.title: Flags in Relation

publicationDetails.detailsText: Raven: A Journal of Vexillology, forthcoming

detail.abstract: Analysis of the aesthetics of flag design should extend beyond considering flags in isolation. It should also appreciate how flags function in conjunction with other flags. Specifically, flags should be understood 1) as representatives of flag design genres; 2) in their hierarchical or functional connections; 3) as constituent parts of physical ensembles of multiple flags; and 4) for their place in historical movements of flag design.

title: Reinforcement Learning-Assisted Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithm for Cyber Risk-Aware Autonomous Ambulance Allocation and Routing: A 2025 Los Angeles Wildfire Case Study
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Tecnológico de Monterrey - Escuela de Ingenieria y Ciencias, University of Ottawa and Tecnológico de Monterrey

detail.title: Reinforcement Learning-Assisted Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithm for Cyber Risk-Aware Autonomous Ambulance Allocation and Routing: A 2025 Los Angeles Wildfire Case Study
detail.abstract: The rise of autonomous vehicles (AVs) in transportation holds promise for revolutionizing emergency healthcare logistics. Ambulance allocation and routing is a real-time, dynamic, NP-hard problem complicated further by cyber-physical vulnerabilities that may disrupt communication and operational reliability. This study formulates the cyber risk-aware Autonomous Ambulance Allocation and Routing Problem (AARP) as a weighted multi-objective optimization problem, minimizing a composite of patient service completion times and delay penalties across priority tiers, while accounting for cyber-induced service interruptions through a robust disruption-budget model grounded in reliability engineering parameters. To solve this problem, we propose Q2GA, a reinforcement learning-assisted quantum-inspired genetic algorithm that dynamically tunes rotation-gate parameters via an ε-greedy Q-learning controller, enhancing exploration and exploitation without manual parameter scheduling. Unlike fixed-angle quantum genetic algorithms, Q2GA adapts its rotation policy based on population diversity and fitness signals, enabling more effective navigation of complex solution spaces. Benchmarked against a standard GA, Simulated Annealing, and a baseline QGA across three instance scales, Q2GA achieves the best mean solution quality on the small and medium instances; on the large instance its mean is statistically indistinguishable from that of simulated annealing, and its advantage shifts from mean fitness to run-to-run consistency. Sensitivity analysis reveals that disruption scope has a larger system-wide impact than recovery duration, a finding with direct implications for fleet cyber-resilience strategy. A simulation case study based on the 2025 Los Angeles Palisades Fire, combining real road-network geometry and reported infrastructure outages with simulated patients, triage classes and disruptions, evaluates the framework under geographically heterogeneous disruption conditions, where Q2GA exhibits the least performance degradation among all algorithms. The source code and simulation metadata are openly available; see the Data Availability statement.

title: Structural Origination and Creation Capability: Authoring Competitive Terrain in an AI-Driven World
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Structural Origination and Creation Capability: Authoring Competitive Terrain in an AI-Driven World
detail.abstract:
The most consequential strategic question in a world of continuous structural transformation is not whether organizations can recognize emerging competitive logics or respond to them effectively. It is whether they can author the governing premises of the next structural plane before others define it — and in doing so determine the logic within which competition subsequently unfolds. Existing strategy and organization theory has built substantial explanatory power around the problem of response: how organizations sense, adapt, reconstruct, and reposition once structural change becomes recognizable. What this tradition does not specify is the prior condition that determines whether adaptation is the only option available or whether authorship remains structurally possible.

Building on the Integrating Structure and Life Energy (ISLE) framework, the article establishes that structural transformation originates prior to field-level recognition — as ideational variation within perceptual systems — and that the interval between origination and field-level visibility is the only interval in which the governing premises of the next structural plane remain open for construction rather than adaptation. It introduces interpretive foresight as the structural condition — not a cognitive capability but an emergent architectural property — that determines whether a perceptual entity can engage that interval before it closes. Interpretive foresight is perishable: it is continuously eroded by the same consolidation processes that generate organizational success, making its deliberate construction and preservation a prior strategic imperative.

Interpretive foresight creates a foresight decision point that existing theory does not specify: a temporally bounded bifurcation between perpetuation — directing developmental capacity toward reconstructing interpretive authority within the plane others are constructing — and exploration — using the foresight window to originate a structural plane that renders the emerging competitive terrain a secondary contest. The article develops structural origination as the capacity to construct the governing premises of a structural plane that does not yet exist, specifies the Perpetuator and Explorer as categorically distinct archetypes, and introduces creation capability — high sensing intelligence, high permeability, and flexible structures anchored in purpose rather than premises — as the organizational configuration under which structural origination becomes possible.

Artificial intelligence intensifies the asymmetry between these orientations. For Perpetuator-archetype entities, AI reinforces incumbent premises while compressing the reconstruction interval on which perpetuation depends. For Explorer-archetype entities with maintained interpretive elasticity, AI functions as the primary instrument of construction itself — enabling second-order origination: the capacity to construct a new structural plane while designing the conditions for that plane's own future reconstruction. Under conditions of AI-driven continuous structural transformation — in which structural planes may be generated faster than any single plane can consolidate — response-based competitive advantage reaches its structural limit. Creation capability shifts under these conditions from a source of competitive advantage to the condition of sustained competitive existence.

title: Two-Phase Phase-Type Queues: Closed-Form Distributions and the Numerical Accuracy Landscape of BuTools

detail.title: Two-Phase Phase-Type Queues: Closed-Form Distributions and the Numerical Accuracy Landscape of BuTools

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: Two-phase phase-type (P H 2) queues occupy a unique position in queueing theory: flexible enough to capture both low-and high-variability service processes, yet structured enough to admit complete algebraic characterization. Despite their prevalence in telecommunications, healthcare, and manufacturing, their explicit steady-state and sojourn-time distributions have not been collected in a single treatment with systematic numerical validation. We derive closed-form queuelength distributions p n = A 1 r n 1 + A 2 r n 2 and sojourn-time densities for the complete M/P H 2 /1 family (Erlang-2, hypoexponential-2, hyperexponential-2, and Coxian-2), with all coefficients given as explicit functions of system parameters. Comprehensive validation against BuTools maps the numerical accuracy landscape of matrix-analytic computation: queue-length evaluation achieves machine-precision accuracy across extreme parameter ranges (ρ up to 0.999, C 2 s exceeding 10,000), while sojourn-time evaluation via the matrix exponential loses up to 10 significant digits when high traffic intensity and high service variability act jointly. The symbolic expressions enable analytical operations inaccessible to numerical output: exact sensitivity analysis, closed-form threshold optimization, and rigorous tail-probability guarantees. We prove that P H 2 marks the boundary of algebraic tractability: even the simplest three-phase queue (M/E 3 /1) has a universally negative discriminant, forcing complex roots at every traffic intensity, so that its distribution cannot be expressed as a sum of real geometric terms. For k ≥ 5 phases, the Abel-Ruffini theorem precludes radical solutions entirely. The results serve as a ready-to-use reference for two-phase service models.

title: A Benchmark for Measuring How Much a Strategy’s Performance Moves When the Market Environment Is Varied, Rather Than How High It Is on the One Environment That Happened to Occur

detail.title: A Benchmark for Measuring How Much a Strategy’s Performance Moves When the Market Environment Is Varied, Rather Than How High It Is on the One Environment That Happened to Occur
detail.abstract: A backtest is one draw from a distribution of histories that never got run. Indian equity markets over our study window contain roughly one pandemic crash, one full rate cycle and one structural liquidity shift, so a claim that a strategy is “robust across regimes” rests on a handful of effective observations no matter how many sessions were simulated. Paper 1 of this programme asked whether a machine-written strategy is real. The survivors it handed forward survived one sequence of events, and that is a weaker claim than it looks. We release RegimeStress: a benchmark for measuring how much a strategy’s performance moves when the environment changes. It provides a causally-labelled regime series over 1,233 sessions, estimated by expanding-window refits with a forward-only decode so that no label uses information from after the session it describes; Counterfactual Regime Resampling, a stationary block bootstrap conditioned on regime label that manufactures plausible histories that did not happen; a moment-validation suite those synthetic histories must pass; two stress tiers of very different cost; and a frozen strategy population whose exclusion rules were fixed before any stress path was run. The central methodological result: a shortcut reproduced performance and did not reproduce fragility. Resampling a strategy’s realised returns agrees with full counterfactual re-simulation at Spearman 0.897 on mean performance but only 0.620 on fragility (n = 125), and fragility is the quantity of interest. A second shortcut, measured the same way, holds at 0.963 and is adopted. Shortcut safety is an experiment here, not a design decision. The benchmark’s first prediction task is a null, and we diagnose it rather than report it bare. Fragility cannot be predicted from strategy characteristics at this sample size: five models on identical folds reach an out-of-sample R2 of +0.024 across 109 strategies and 26 features. A permutation test nonetheless rejects the null for the ranking while failing to reject it for the level. Trained unchanged and applied to 60 strategies from three frontier models as held-out data, the predictor reaches R2 = −0.004: no better than a constant. The failure is a property of the problem, not of one small model’s output. Fragility itself proved generator-independent, every frontier arm’s median landing within a sixth of the local corpus’s, while one measured pathology did not recur at all.

title: Caring across cultures: A qualitative study of the workforce challenges and organizational issues of CALD aged care workers in Australia’s residential aged care sector
affiliations: Fudan University

detail.title: Caring across cultures: A qualitative study of the workforce challenges and organizational issues of CALD aged care workers in Australia’s residential aged care sector

keywords.keywords: Cultural diversity in the Australian residential aged care workforce: Challenges and opportunities.

detail.abstract: The elderly care workforce in Australia is becoming more culturally and linguistically diverse, underscoring the need to understand better the viewpoints of Culturally and Linguistically Diverse (CALD) workers in residential aged care. This qualitative descriptive study used semi-structured interviews with 38 CALD aged care providers across four Australian states. The findings show that organizational structures, cultural differences, and language barriers are important determinants of daily care practices and interactions with CALD patients. Cultural misunderstandings that caused emotional anguish and tiredness, and communication problems that affected the quality of therapy, were cited by respondents. The biggest barriers to culturally sensitive treatment were severe workloads, staff shortages, inflexible workplace policies, and limited access to culturally appropriate training. Employees also highlighted more fundamental structural concerns, such as a lack of funds and insufficient government policies to encourage culturally inclusive aged care services. Participants indicated the need for greater organizational support, more flexible person-centered care practices, and more cultural competence training. The report recommends measures to address labor shortages, workplace discrimination and legislative barriers to support CALD workers and improve the cultural safety and quality of elder care services in Australia.

title: From Deep Learning to Real-World Surveillance: A Case Study of Flock Safety's Automated License Plate Recognition Network

detail.title: From Deep Learning to Real-World Surveillance: A Case Study of Flock Safety's Automated License Plate Recognition Network

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: n/a
declarations.funderStatement: n/a

detail.abstract: This case study examines automated license plate recognition (ALPR) as a real-world application of deep learning, using Flock Safety, the largest ALPR provider in the United States, as the primary example. It first explains how convolutional neural networks (CNNs) make high-volume, unstructured image recognition possible, then examines how the technology has actually been used since its nationwide rollout. The study documents three governance failures: the use of local camera data for federal immigration enforcement without the knowledge or consent of the cities that installed the cameras; documented cases of individual officers using the system to track romantic partners and other private citizens; and weak transparency structures that allowed both problems to persist largely undetected until victims or journalists uncovered them independently. It also examines the company's response to these incidents, the resulting wave of contract cancellations and lawsuits, and the more informal public backlash that has included direct destruction of camera hardware. The study argues that the model's core technical performance is not the source of these harms; the harms stem from a governance and accountability gap between what the system is technically capable of and the safeguards built around its use. It concludes with concrete recommendations for closing that gap, drawing on prior work on purpose limitation and algorithmic auditing.

title: Praxeology and Analytic Philosophy of Action
affiliations: Queen's University Belfast and University of Warsaw

detail.title: Praxeology and Analytic Philosophy of Action
detail.abstract: This chapter reconstructs Tadeusz Kotarbiński's praxeology as a systematic and original contribution to analytic philosophy of action. Rather than treating praxeology as a marginal or historical doctrine of efficiency, the chapter presents it as a philosophical framework for analysing rational and purposive action. Its full import becomes visible only when set alongside later debates that, independently arrived at, converge on questions that praxeology had already posed. It begins by distinguishing three historical traditions: the French project of a general science of action, the Austrian school, and the Polish school developed by Kotarbiński, the most systematic and philosophically advanced of the three. The chapter then places Kotarbiński's praxeology within the intellectual context of the Lvov-Warsaw School. It shows how its ideals of clarity and rigor, together with Kotarbiński's ontology, informed his account of agency-and how this account carries an ethical dimension, expressed in the ideals of good work and the reliable guardian (that have no equivalent in the French or Austrian traditions). By reading Kotarbiński together with Anscombe, Davidson, and Bratman, the chapter shows that praxeology anticipates and converges in striking ways with later debates about the nature of action, while preserving its distinctive normative orientation. The chapter concludes that praxeology can enrich philosophy of action and contribute to organisation theory by addressing the long-recognised gap between theory and practice.

title: Trust and Social Networks: Citius, Altius, Fortius
affiliations: , University of Arizona, and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Trust and Social Networks: Citius, Altius, Fortius

declarations.funderStatement: This chapter was supported by the National Science Foundation under CAREER Award 1943688 to Oliver Schilke.

detail.abstract: Trust and social networks are deeply intertwined. Yet the two literatures have developed largely in parallel. Trust research has remained largely focused on dyads, network research on structure. This introductory chapter makes the case for integration. Trust scholarship gains when trust relations are treated as structurally embedded rather than socially isolated. Network scholarship, on the other hand, gains a relational mechanism that converts structural opportunity into meaningful social action. To clarify the interface and provide a systematic foundation for cumulative inquiry, we offer a tripartite typology of trust-network theorizing: (1) trust as a network property; (2) the co-evolution of trust and networks; and (3) the interdependent effects of trust and networks. We close by using the typology to organize the contributions to this Handbook and to identify opportunities for research at the nexus of trust and networks.

title: Distributionally Robust Dynamic Optimization for Urban Water Recycling Operations
affiliations: , Zhejiang University - School of Management and Wilfrid Laurier University - School of Business & Economics

detail.title: Distributionally Robust Dynamic Optimization for Urban Water Recycling Operations
detail.abstract: Urban water-recycling systems dynamically balance wastewater recycling and primary water production to ensure efficient and reliable water supply. However, this task faces prominent supply-demand mismatches driven by fluctuating demand, volatile wastewater inflows, and persistent environmental conditions. Methodology/results: We formulate these operational decisions by a finite-horizon dynamic model under distributional ambiguity. We capture environmental signals using exogenous Markov covariates (e.g., rainfall, streamflow, and temperature), and decompose demand and wastewater inflows into covariate-dependent predictions with uncertain residuals. Analytically, we show that the worst-case distribution is countermonotonic and can be computed offline, thereby reducing the robust dynamic problem to a standard dynamic program. Furthermore, the optimal robust policy retains a covariate-dependent threshold structure. Practically, using Melbourne Water data, we show that our approach reallocates precautionary production across environmental regimes while hedging against residual distributional ambiguity and adverse demand-inflow dependence. As a result, it substantially reduces average out-of-sample operating costs and exposure to extreme-cost outcomes while mitigating severe shortages. Managerial implications: As current system states and decisions shape the ability to absorb future demand-inflow mismatches, day-today operating decisions for water production and recycling are inherently forward-looking. Observable environmental signals can be used to position the system ahead of adverse regimes, while distributional robustness further protects the resulting dynamic plan against residual uncertainty. Our framework shows that such robust and efficient decisions can be implemented dynamically through simple and interpretable policies. More importantly, beyond its environmental benefits, water recycling creates operational value as an intertemporal buffer that helps managers prepare for future misalignment between recyclable supply and service demand.

reference: Robert Diab, "Is There a Constitutional Right to a Human Decision in Canada?" (2026) 35:1 Constitutional Forum 19.
title: Is There a Constitutional Right to a Human Decision in Canada?
affiliations: Thompson Rivers University - Faculty of Law

detail.title: Is There a Constitutional Right to a Human Decision in Canada?

publicationDetails.detailsText: Robert Diab, "Is There a Constitutional Right to a Human Decision in Canada?" (2026) 35:1 Constitutional Forum 19.

detail.abstract: In the mid-2010s, government interest in and uptake of automated decision-making prompted debate over law and policy on point. At issue were forms of AI that did not give reasons and relied on algorithms of varying degrees of opacity. Canada's Treasury Board Directive on Automated Decision-Making and Guide on the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence follow the EU's GDPR and AI Act in recognizing rights to a human decision and to an explanation of automated decision-making, thereby limiting the use of AI in high-impact cases. But recent advances in AI challenge the assumptions underlying this approach. Language models can generate reasons for a decision comparable in quality to those of a human-prompting a need to look beyond existing law and policy toward constitutional limits on use of this technology. This article outlines the contours of Charter rights to a human decision and an explanation, which, for the foreseeable future, preclude significant reliance on language models in high-impact administrative cases regardless of their capabilities.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Scientific Search, and Symmetric Standards
affiliations: Åbo Akademi University, Finland

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence, Scientific Search, and Symmetric Standards
detail.abstract:
This article develops a theory of scientific search and symmetric standards for comprehensive artificial-intelligence cooperation in research. It is not an empirical evaluation of a particular AI system, but a theoretical account of how scientific work should be assessed when AI contributes substantively to question formation, hypothesis generation, cross-disciplinary comparison, criticism, epistemic salvage, verification design, and scholarly expression.

The central claim is that AI’s scientific importance lies not only in accelerating existing tasks, but in changing what becomes practically investigable under finite resources. Restricting available analytical capacity is therefore itself a research strategy, with opportunity costs and foregone scientific value. The framework distinguishes generation, pursuit, warrant, and portfolio allocation, allowing broad exploratory search while preserving exact standards for final claims.

The article argues for symmetric scientific standards: evaluation should follow claim type, consequence, risk, evidential basis, and method-specific vulnerability rather than the degree of AI contribution. A3-level contribution is treated as a descriptive classification, not a scientific defect. Extensive AI contribution may require fuller disclosure, but it should not create an independent quality penalty.

The governing norm is disciplined ambition: use available analytical capacity at the level that best advances consequential inquiry under symmetric substantive standards and complete human responsibility.

reference: CESifo Working Paper No. 12904
title: The Labor Market Effects of Expanding Overtime Coverage
affiliations: University of Southern California

detail.title: The Labor Market Effects of Expanding Overtime Coverage
detail.abstract: This paper examines the labor market effects of overtime coverage in the United States, where salaried workers are covered for overtime if their base pay falls below a legislated salary threshold. Using an event-study design with administrative payroll data and state-level threshold changes from 2014-2021, I find evidence against conventional models of overtime. Contrary to the historical intent of policymakers, firms do not increase employment by substituting more workers for fewer hours. However, contrary to compensating differential models, firms also do not offset the costs of overtime by lowering workers' base pays. Instead, employers raised salaries above the threshold to keep workers exempt from overtime, indicating that monitoring and adjusting workers' hours is costly for firms. Taken together, these results suggest that expanding overtime coverage increases workers' earnings without negatively impacting employment.

title: Outsourcing to Poland: Cost Advantages, Strategic Opportunities, and Challenges for U.S. Companies
affiliations: University of Central Asia (UCA)

detail.title: Outsourcing to Poland: Cost Advantages, Strategic Opportunities, and Challenges for U.S. Companies
detail.abstract: This study examines the outsourcing practices of U.S. companies operating in Poland, with particular attention to the cost-saving advantages, strategic opportunities, and operational challenges involved. Outsourcing has traditionally been understood primarily as a cost-cutting strategy; however, over the past two decades it has evolved into a more complex practice through which firms seek specialized talent, service quality, and favorable strategic positioning. Poland has emerged as a significant outsourcing hub, offering not only cost savings but also strategic access to the European market. Using a qualitative-descriptive research design supported by secondary quantitative data, this study compares wages, operational expenses, and businessenvironment indicators between the United States and Poland. The findings show that U.S. firms can achieve substantial labor-cost savings, reaching as much as 62% in some industries, alongside the benefits of Poland's well-developed information and communication technology (ICT) sector, high literacy rate, and favorable trading environment. At the same time, outsourcing to Poland is associated with challenges such as regulatory complexity, rising electricity costs, and cultural differences. The study concludes that Poland represents an attractive outsourcing destination, particularly for knowledge-intensive industries, provided that firms plan carefully to mitigate entry barriers and operational risks. These findings contribute to the academic literature on international outsourcing and offer practical guidance for managerial decision-making in global outsourcing strategy.

title: Optimal Mechanisms with Hierarchically Interdependent Values
affiliations: Northwestern University - Department of Managerial Economics and Decision Sciences (MEDS)

detail.title: Optimal Mechanisms with Hierarchically Interdependent Values
detail.abstract:
I study optimal allocation under hierarchical interdependence. In the
baseline model, an incumbent observes a signal that affects both her value and
an entrant's value, while the entrant privately observes an additional
own-value component. I consider a planner whose objective is a weighted sum of
agents' utilities and collected payments. I characterize the optimal ex post
incentive-compatible and individually rational mechanism for every nonnegative
payment weight. When collected payments receive at least as much weight as
agents' utilities, the optimal mechanism is a score-based auction in which the
entrant's report determines an endogenous threshold for the incumbent and the
incumbent's report remains relevant when she loses. When payments are costly
to the planner, the optimal mechanism instead has a payment-free region in which the
entrant always receives the asset and a screening region in which the agents
compete through a monotone cutoff. For the valuable-payments case, the
score-based characterization extends to environments with multiple agents.
With one incumbent and several entrants,
the optimal mechanism compares the incumbent with the strongest entrant
alternative even when the incumbent's report changes the entrants' ranking. In
a longer ordered hierarchy, the characterization extends under a local virtual
single-crossing condition.

reference: Peterson Institute for International Economics Policy Brief 26-12
title: Made with China: Global Supply Chains and the Limits of US Decoupling
affiliations: Syracuse University Maxwell School and Peterson Institute for International Economics

detail.title: Made with China: Global Supply Chains and the Limits of US Decoupling

publicationDetails.detailsText: Peterson Institute for International Economics Policy Brief 26-12
publicationDetails.journalName: Peterson Institute for International Economics (PIIE) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Using Asian Development Bank multiregional input-output tables for 2007–24, this Policy Brief traces Chinese value added throughout the US import basket. It argues that genuine US economic security requires a more disciplined strategy—identifying actual chokepoints, building competitive alternative suppliers and the infrastructure connecting them to markets, and cooperating with allies rather than forcing them into separate supply chains. The appendix explains the method and databases that the authors used in their analysis.

title: Pakistan Women's Experience in Business Entrepreneurship

detail.title: Pakistan Women's Experience in Business Entrepreneurship
detail.abstract: This paper examines phenomenology as a qualitative research methodology for understanding the lived experiences of Pakistani women entrepreneurs. It focuses on how gender roles, cultural norms, Islamic beliefs, family expectations, and structural barriers shape women's entrepreneurial experiences. The paper reviews descriptive and interpretive phenomenology and explains the relevance of Heidegger's hermeneutic approach to understanding experiences within their social, historical, cultural, and religious contexts. It also outlines the use of purposive sampling, semi-structured interviews, participant language choice, and thematic analysis. Particular attention is given to Islamic influence on business decisions, family support, gender roles, access to finance, mobility restrictions, and work-life balance.
